benefit: RapidScreen RS-2000 helped radiologists spot small lung cancers
developer or vendor: Deus Technologies, LLC (listed as Riverain Medical Group in the FDA database)
AI tool: RapidScreen RS-2000
deployment context: Deus Technologies (reader study with 15 radiologists at Georgetown University Medical Center); Washington, D.C., United States
use-case relevant outcome: the area under the ROC curve rose from 0.8288 to 0.8654
what the sources leave unknown: The gain comes from a reader study on 240 archived films from 1970s screening of male heavy smokers aged 45 or older, read by 15 radiologists, so it does not show results in other patients or in practice. Readers saw each film with the marks right after reading it alone. No patient outcome is reported, and the device had not been marketed.

benefit: Second Look would have cut missed breast cancers by at least a quarter
developer or vendor: CADx Medical Systems, Inc. (listed as iCAD, Inc. in the FDA database)
AI tool: Second Look
deployment context: CADx Medical Systems (ROSE-1 study on earlier screening mammograms from 17 institutions and ROSE-2 study at 5 institutions)
use-case relevant outcome: cut missed cancers on earlier screening mammograms by at least 26.2%
what the sources leave unknown: The 26.2 percent figure is a retrospective estimate from panel readings of old films, and it assumes that 64 unexamined films held visible lesions. No radiologist read those films with the marks. The prospective study measured work-up rates, not cancers found. The system marked 62.7 percent of the missed cancers.

benefit: LUMA imaging found more high-grade cervical lesions after colposcopy
AI tool: LUMA Cervical Imaging System
deployment context: Seven colposcopy centers with 16 colposcopists in the intended use study
what the sources leave unknown: The pivotal study stopped early at 227 of 788 planned women, with 193 evaluable, and FDA's advisory panel recommended that the LUMA system not be approved. A larger randomized study did not show a statistically significant increase in detection. No outcome of treatment for the women is reported.

benefit: MammaPrint separated node-negative breast cancers by risk of spread
AI tool: MammaPrint
deployment context: TRANSBIG consortium (independent validation on tumors from five European centers); Villejuif and Saint-Cloud, France; Stockholm, Sweden; London and Oxford, United Kingdom
use-case relevant outcome: 95% of low risk and 78% of high risk patients were free of distant metastasis
what the sources leave unknown: None of the validation studies involved US patients, and the patient report says that performance in the US population has not been established. The validation used 302 patients diagnosed before 1999. The test is a prognostic marker only, and it is not meant to predict response to therapy or to select therapy. The 5-year rates are from one European patient group.

benefit: Pathwork Tissue of Origin Test matched the known origin of most tumors
AI tool: Pathwork Tissue of Origin Test
deployment context: Pathwork Diagnostics (clinical validation at four processing laboratories)
use-case relevant outcome: 86.3% of metastatic and 92.0% of primary tumor specimens
what the sources leave unknown: The validation compared results with the available diagnosis because no reference standard for diagnostic truth was used. It counted 545 of 659 processed specimens. The test is not intended for tumors that current practice cannot diagnose, nor to predict disease course, survival or treatment efficacy.

benefit: EasyCell's white cell counts track manual microscopy in FDA's review
AI tool: EasyCell Cell Locator (EasyCell)
deployment context: Medica Corporation (method comparison study at three sites); Three study sites (not named in the decision summary)
what the sources leave unknown: The data come from Medica's premarket submission and compare EasyCell with manual microscopy. Technologists reviewed and could change every suggested classification, so the classifier's own accuracy is not reported. The device is intended for skilled operators. The study covered 304 specimens at three sites.

benefit: MelaFind caught nearly all melanomas at low specificity
AI tool: MelaFind
deployment context: Seven dermatology sites in the blinded study (Protocol 20061) and physicians in a web-based reader study (Protocol 20063); Seven dermatology sites, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The pivotal study blinded dermatologists to MelaFind results, so it did not test whether the device changes biopsy decisions. FDA required a post-approval study to evaluate whether MelaFind increases physicians' sensitivity. The reader studies used stored images and patient histories. The pivotal study used only board-certified dermatologists.

benefit: MarginProbe helped surgeons remove cancer left at lumpectomy margins
AI tool: MarginProbe System
deployment context: Surgical sites in the randomized trial in Israel and the United States (596 women undergoing lumpectomy); Israel and United States
what the sources leave unknown: The trial did not note why surgeons took each extra shave, so the device's own contribution was not assessed. The design gave the device arm three chances to shave and the control arm two, a bias that favors the device. The drop in re-operations was not statistically significant. Most patients were treated in Israel, and breast cosmesis was not assessed.

benefit: Amputee with 48 years of phantom limb pain reaches pain-free periods
developer or vendor: Chalmers University of Technology, Biomedical Engineering Division (academic lab; study part-funded by Integrum AB)
AI tool: Phantom motor execution: BioPatRec myoelectric pattern recognition (LDA and MLP classifiers) driving augmented/virtual reality and a racing game
deployment context: Chalmers University of Technology and Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Gothenburg (inferred from author affiliations; the paper does not name the treatment site); Gothenburg, Sweden (inferred from author affiliations)
sample: 81 people with phantom limb pain randomized at 9 outpatient clinics in Sweden, the Netherlands, Slovenia, Ireland, Germany, Canada and the United States.
use-case relevant outcome: after ten weeks near-absent pain developing into completely pain-free periods
what the sources leave unknown: Pain relief was self-reported by one treatment-resistant patient who received combined motor training, augmented reality and gaming. One case cannot isolate the classifier's effect or rule out expectation and other changes at the same time. In the 2024 randomized trial the authors found no evidence that the decoded execution was superior to guided motor imagery.

benefit: VITEK MS identified microbes from patient cultures in five labs
AI tool: VITEK MS (MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry with the Advanced Spectrum Classifier)
deployment context: Five US clinical microbiology laboratories in the prospective clinical study; Five clinical microbiology laboratories, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The study that bioMérieux submitted measured VITEK MS identifications against molecular sequencing. FDA describes faster identification and earlier appropriate antibiotics only as possible benefits, and the study measured neither time to result nor patient outcomes. Correct single identifications were lower for Gram-negative bacteria, at 83.8%.

benefit: Cologuard caught more colorectal cancers than a standard stool test
AI tool: Cologuard
deployment context: Exact Sciences (DeeP-C study at 90 sites in the United States and Canada); 90 sites in the United States and Canada
use-case relevant outcome: detected 92.3% of colorectal cancers against 73.8% for FIT
what the sources leave unknown: The pivotal study was cross-sectional, so it measured detection against colonoscopy and not later cancer outcomes. It compared Cologuard with one brand of FIT. The cancer sensitivity rests on 65 cancers. Cologuard was not evaluated in people with a history of colorectal cancer, adenomas or related cancers.

benefit: Ahead 100 EEG test missed its goals but helped rule out injury on CT
AI tool: BrainScope Ahead 100 (Models CV-100 and M-100)
deployment context: BrainScope (B-AHEAD II study at 11 US emergency department sites); Eleven emergency department sites, United States
use-case relevant outcome: negative predictive value for injury on CT was 89.5%
what the sources leave unknown: The B-AHEAD II study missed both accuracy endpoints. FDA raised concerns about missing data, with 123 patients lacking a classification, and about how the need for CT was judged. Patients with a Glasgow score of 15 who did not meet the New Orleans Criteria counted as CT negative without a scan. Physicians never saw the Ahead 100 output, so the 29% figure rests on assumptions.

benefit: Exomiser ranks gene variants to help diagnose rare disease in England
developer or vendor: Queen Mary University of London (Exomiser team led by Damian Smedley)
AI tool: Exomiser phenotype-driven variant prioritization (machine-learning-assisted scoring and ranking)
deployment context: Genomics England and NHS Genomic Medicine Centers; England, United Kingdom
use-case relevant outcome: Genetic diagnoses were found in 25% of probands, rising to 35% for monogenic disorders
what the sources leave unknown: The pilot's diagnostic yield and clinical actionability apply to the combined workflow of sequencing, panels, prioritization and clinical review. They cannot all be attributed to Exomiser. The authors do not say whether Exomiser or the applied panels found the variants in the two patient cases that they describe. Changes in clinical decisions do not show better health or survival across the pilot.

benefit: Superpower Glass briefly raises social scores of children with autism
developer or vendor: Stanford University (Wall lab, Division of Systems Medicine and Department of Computer Science)
AI tool: Superpower Glass: Google Glass with a real-time machine-learning facial emotion classifier and companion smartphone app
deployment context: Participating families at home under the Stanford studies; Palo Alto, United States
use-case relevant outcome: gained 4.58 points more on the Vineland socialization subscale than controls (P = .005)
what the sources leave unknown: The reports of eye contact and the change in scores in the feasibility study had no controls. The trial's advantage concerns one of four primary measures and the whole home intervention, including family interaction. Spectrum reported that the Vineland gain had disappeared six weeks after treatment ended, and the authors of the 2024 review flag low adherence and potential funding bias.

benefit: Embrace wristband alerts a mother, who calls paramedics
AI tool: Empatica Embrace wrist-worn seizure detection (electrodermal activity and accelerometer, on-board algorithm) with the Alert smartphone app
deployment context: Fulton, Missouri, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The rescue rests on a single news account, and no clinical record of the event has been found. The same article covers a death despite a successful alert, which shows that a timely human response is a separate requirement.

benefit: QVCAD cut reading time for breast ultrasound by a third
AI tool: QVCAD System
deployment context: QView Medical (reader study with 18 radiologists on 185 automated breast ultrasound cases); United States
what the sources leave unknown: The reader study was retrospective and used 185 existing screening exams from 2009 and 2010, of which 52 showed cancer. Readers worked in a setting built to mimic clinical reading, not in practice. Accuracy was slightly lower with QVCAD, though within the margin. Gains in patient throughput and wider use of breast ultrasound are FDA's expectations, not measurements.

benefit: EyeArt could halve retinal grading and miss no high-risk retinopathy
AI tool: EyeArt
deployment context: Three NHS diabetic eye screening programs in England (North East London, South East London and Gloucestershire), in a research evaluation run in parallel with usual care; North East London, South East London and Gloucestershire, England, United Kingdom
use-case relevant outcome: 15,091 of 30,405, would still have needed human grading
what the sources leave unknown: EyeArt ran in parallel with usual care, so no grader workload or patient outcome was measured. The reference standard was the human grade under the national protocol. The test covered one software version at three English programs in early 2017, and about half of the episodes would still have needed human grading.

benefit: Machine learning helps price Zimbabwe's health financing package
AI tool: Machine-learning-based optimization tool for pricing interventions in Zimbabwe's results-based financing package (not named in the review)
deployment context: Zimbabwe's results-based financing program under the Ministry of Health and Child Care, with Cordaid as project implementation entity (the review does not say who ran the price reviews); Zimbabwe
what the sources leave unknown: The evaluators give the tool one sentence. They do not name it, show its method, say who built it, or give any figure for what it changed in prices, review costs or services. The efficiency rating rests on the project's overall cost-effectiveness combined with implementation inefficiencies, not on the tool.

benefit: PowerLook Tomo cut radiologists' reading time on 3D mammograms
AI tool: iCAD PowerLook Tomo Detection Software
deployment context: iCAD (reader study with 20 radiologists on 240 GE tomosynthesis cases); San Antonio, Texas, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The pivotal study was a retrospective reading of 240 selected exams by several readers, not clinical practice. FDA notes significant limitations, including missing one-year follow-up for some exams and the exclusion of 50 exams, which delayed approval. Reading time and accuracy were analyzed separately. Average specificity fell slightly with the software.

benefit: Kyukyu VoiceTra translates for ambulance crews across Japan
developer or vendor: NICT (National Institute of Information and Communications Technology) with the Fire and Disaster Management Agency and its Fire Research Center
AI tool: Kyukyu VoiceTra (救急ボイストラ): multilingual speech-translation app for ambulance crews built on NICT's VoiceTra engine, 15 languages, 46 fixed phrases
deployment context: Fire headquarters across Japan (Sapporo Fire Department from February 2017; Ninomiya Town fire service from 2022); Japan (fire headquarters nationwide)
sample: Sapporo Fire Bureau ambulance crews who used the app from January 2017. The number of respondents is not given.
use-case relevant outcome: 690 of Japan's 720 fire headquarters (95.8%) used the app
what the sources leave unknown: The fire services have not documented an outcome for a foreign patient, and no independent test of the translation's accuracy appears in the sources. The crews' views come from one survey in Sapporo. The general VoiceTra download figures are not adoption counts for Kyukyu VoiceTra.

benefit: Nevisense caught nearly all melanomas at low specificity
AI tool: Nevisense (electrical impedance spectroscopy with a trained lesion classifier)
deployment context: Dermatology sites in the SIMPS study in Europe and the United States, and 41 US dermatologists in a reader study; Twenty-two dermatology sites in Europe and the United States
what the sources leave unknown: The pivotal study enrolled lesions that physicians had chosen to excise, while the device is meant for lesions before the biopsy decision. Dermatologists were blinded to the device readings. The reader study used 141 lesion images. Melanoma prevalence of 13.7% may exceed that in dermatologists' practices. Of the participants, 97.5% were White.

benefit: An autonomous eye exam passed its trial in primary care clinics
AI tool: IDx-DR
deployment context: Ten primary care sites in the IDx-DR pivotal trial; Ten primary care sites, United States
sample: 900 adults with diabetes enrolled at 10 US primary care sites, of whom 819 were fully analyzable.
what the sources leave unknown: IDx, LLC, the maker, funded the trial. Its primary outcomes were sensitivity and specificity. Accuracy studies of this kind do not report how many more patients would be screened or reach a full eye exam. Enrollment of people with high HbA1c was targeted for part of the study. Of 892 participants, 73 could not be fully analyzed.

benefit: QuantX gave radiologists a small gain on breast MRI
AI tool: QuantX
deployment context: Quantitative Insights (reader study with 19 radiologists); United States
what the sources leave unknown: FDA reviewers write that the study marginally met its primary endpoint, and a second AUC method gave an interval that crossed zero. The test set was enriched and retrospective. Training materials may have biased readers toward QuantX, and 13 examinations came from an earlier study. Individual readers in practice may not see a significant improvement.

benefit: Advanced RBC Application sorted red cells close to manual microscopy
AI tool: Advanced RBC Application (CellaVision DM96 and DM1200)
deployment context: CellaVision (method comparison studies at five clinical sites); Five clinical sites, two in the United States and three outside it
what the sources leave unknown: The studies measured agreement with manual microscopy, not effects on diagnosis or lab time. Operators reviewed and changed the suggested results, so the networks' own accuracy is not reported. The five sites used different comparison methods. The data come from the maker's premarket submission.

benefit: A learning controller makes a prosthetic arm easier to use at home
developer or vendor: Center for Bionic Medicine, Shirley Ryan AbilityLab (formerly the Rehabilitation Institute of Chicago), with Northwestern University
AI tool: Myoelectric pattern recognition control (machine-learning classification of residual-limb EMG) on a custom transhumeral prosthesis built from commercially available parts
deployment context: Center for Bionic Medicine, Shirley Ryan AbilityLab, with home use by trial participants; Chicago, Illinois, United States (laboratory testing) and participants' homes
sample: Eight transhumeral amputees with TMR, Center for Bionic Medicine, Chicago.
use-case relevant outcome: moved three clothespins in 90.2 seconds on average against 137 seconds with direct control
what the sources leave unknown: The trial had eight participants, all men, after a ninth withdrew. Assignment of the order of control methods was not blinded. Each method was used at home for at least six weeks. The team that developed the surgery and the control method ran the trial, and two of its members have a financial interest in Coapt, which sells myoelectric control systems. Two of four tests showed no significant difference.

benefit: ContaCT alerts came sooner than usual care in a test on past scans
AI tool: ContaCT
deployment context: Viz.ai (standalone performance test on archived CT angiograms); Two clinical sites, United States
sample: 300 archived CT angiograms, including 44 true positive cases with usual-care times.
what the sources leave unknown: Viz.ai ran a retrospective standalone test on 300 past CT angiograms from two US sites, so no alert reached a specialist and no patient outcome was measured. FDA notes that the time comparison may involve some bias because it could only use the subset of true positive scans that had a recorded usual-care notification time.

benefit: Dexcom G6's Urgent Low Soon alert may cut time below 54 mg/dL
AI tool: Dexcom G6 real-time continuous glucose monitoring system, 'Urgent Low Soon' predictive low glucose alert (also present on the G7 in one independent study)
deployment context: United States (vendor analyses); London, United Kingdom (Imperial College trials)
sample: Study 1: Six hospitals in Belgium and 254 adults with type 1 diabetes who already used FreeStyle Libre, recruited 29 January to 30 July 2019. Study 2: Users in Germany, Sweden and the United Kingdom who switched from G5 to G6 9 to 12 months after the G6 launch in each country. They were followed in a two-year window from 2018 to 2020.
use-case relevant outcome: time below 54 mg/dL fell from 1.0% to 0.6%
what the sources leave unknown: No study isolates the alert in routine use. Dexcom's analyses compare the same users before and after the switch without a control arm, and the Imperial switch study and the ALERTT1 trial change the whole device. The 2022 authors could not test whether the alert changed outcomes, and the prediction algorithm is proprietary.

benefit: OsteoDetect helped clinicians find wrist fractures on X-rays
AI tool: OsteoDetect
deployment context: Imagen Technologies (reader study with 24 clinicians); United States
sample: 24 clinicians of six types and 200 cases.
what the sources leave unknown: The 24 clinicians read archived wrist X-rays through a web interface, not in a clinic, so OsteoDetect guided no care and no patient outcome was measured. Accuracy was judged only on what is visible in one radiograph. The aided gain cannot be separated from how the output was displayed. The authors are affiliated with Imagen, which funded the study.

benefit: Surgery-length predictions shortened patient waits at Sloan Kettering
developer or vendor: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center (Department of Strategy and Innovation)
AI tool: Memorial Sloan Kettering machine learning surgical case-duration prediction model
deployment context: Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center; Memorial Sloan Kettering main campus and Josie Robertson Surgical Center, New York, United States
sample: 683 colorectal and gynecology cases on two Memorial Sloan Kettering campuses.
use-case relevant outcome: fell by 33.1 minutes per patient, from 49.4 to 16.3 minutes
what the sources leave unknown: Memorial Sloan Kettering's own staff built the model and ran the trial at one center in two surgical services. The accuracy gain for gynecology operations was not significant. Wait time was measured only for the patient who followed the first operation in a room. The usual estimates ran about half an hour short, and Dexter and Epstein argued that adjusting for that bias could match the model.

benefit: MATRx plus identified apnea patients who did well with a mouthpiece
AI tool: MATRx plus
deployment context: Zephyr Sleep Technologies (home study in adults with mild to moderate obstructive sleep apnea)
what the sources leave unknown: The MATRx plus study judged success by one night's automated home sleep test with the custom appliance, not by symptoms or long-term outcomes. Few participants were non-responders, so the confidence intervals for specificity (0.40 to 1.00) and negative predictive value (0.34 to 1.00) were wide. The study was the maker's own submission to FDA.

benefit: Software detects more cardiac arrests than Copenhagen dispatchers do
AI tool: Corti machine-learning call-analysis framework for out-of-hospital cardiac arrest recognition (the peer-reviewed papers describe it only as a machine learning framework, and the EENA report names Corti)
deployment context: Copenhagen Emergency Medical Services, Emergency Medical Dispatch Center Copenhagen; Copenhagen, Denmark
what the sources leave unknown: The model's higher sensitivity does not show that the dispatch work improved, because the trial found no significant gain in how often dispatchers recognized arrests. In a review of 2026, the authors rated the trial as having some concerns for risk of bias. The trial authors do not report an outcome for a single patient.

benefit: Medicare credits ContaCT with faster stroke alerts in a payment review
AI tool: ContaCT (Viz LVO algorithm with Viz Hub and Viz View)
deployment context: US hospitals using ContaCT, including SkyRidge Medical Center, Wellstar, Methodist Le Bonheur Healthcare and Mount Sinai Health System; United States
sample: Study 1: SkyRidge (32 patients), Wellstar (120 patients), Methodist Le Bonheur (46 patients), Mount Sinai (42 patients). Study 2: Past scans from the study submitted for FDA authorization.
use-case relevant outcome: the median time to notification was 4.31 minutes
what the sources leave unknown: CMS relied on information that Viz.ai provided. The FDA figures came from standalone testing of ContaCT on past scans. The door-to-puncture reductions came from three unpublished single-center retrospective reviews. The routine-use median of 4.31 minutes is company data. No randomized comparison or published outcome study is cited.

benefit: LensHooke X1 let lay users measure sperm concentration accurately
AI tool: LensHooke X1 and X1 PRO Semen Quality Analyzer
deployment context: Bonraybio (user performance study with 100 lay users at three evaluation sites)
use-case relevant outcome: a slope of 0.98 and an R2 of 0.98
what the sources leave unknown: The lay-user study ran at three evaluation sites, one of them internal, not in users' homes. The reference was another automated analyzer, the SQA-V. Agreement for morphology was weaker, with a slope of 0.78 and an R2 of 0.73. FDA notes that the LensHooke X1 does not give a comprehensive evaluation of a man's fertility.

benefit: EyeBOX missed its goals for accuracy but helped rule out concussion
AI tool: EyeBOX
deployment context: Oculogica (clinical study in 282 patients with head injury)
what the sources leave unknown: The study measured EyeBOX's accuracy against a clinical reference standard, not patient outcomes, and the investigators revised that standard partway through because clinicians were so often uncertain. The device missed both of its accuracy goals, a lower confidence limit above 70 percent for sensitivity and for specificity. FDA's labeling states that not all patients with concussion show eye tracking abnormalities.

benefit: SkinVision flags a changing mole that proves to be a stage 1A melanoma
AI tool: SkinVision skin-check app (AI analysis of smartphone photographs of moles, graded low, medium or high risk)
deployment context: London, United Kingdom
use-case relevant outcome: stage 1A melanoma was found and removed, and he is cancer-free
what the sources leave unknown: The account depends on the patient's report of the app's warning, the diagnosis and his recovery. No clinician confirms it, and neither the app's output nor a dated medical record appears in the sources. Removing a melanoma early does not prove that the app prevented a death.

benefit: Software detects necrosis in meningioma images in university research
developer or vendor: International Institute of Information Technology Bangalore (IIIT Bangalore)
AI tool: IIIT Bangalore necrosis-detection pipeline
deployment context: Bengaluru, India
what the sources leave unknown: The account names Adaboost and logistic regression as the best models and gives no accuracy figures. The authors describe limited data sets and limited class labels. No use by pathologists, effect on diagnosis or patient outcome has been reported.

benefit: An early warning helps Amsterdam anesthetists keep blood pressure up
AI tool: Hypotension Prediction Index (HPI)
deployment context: Amsterdam UMC, location AMC; Amsterdam UMC, location AMC, Amsterdam, the Netherlands
sample: Study 1: 68 randomized, 60 analyzed adults in elective noncardiac surgery, one tertiary center, May 2018 to March 2019. Study 2: 34 patients having esophageal or lung resection at one hospital in Zagreb, Croatia.
use-case relevant outcome: median time in hypotension fell from 32.7 to 8.0 minutes per patient
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was preliminary, unblinded, single-center and small, and it measured a physiological outcome, not a clinical one. It tested the index together with a treatment protocol, so it cannot separate their effects. Edwards Lifesciences, which makes the index, funded it. Its patients were sicker than a general population. Independent authors say the index's predictive performance may be overestimated.

benefit: Apple Watch heart-rate alarms lead doctors to find atrial fibrillation
AI tool: Apple Watch heart-rate notifications, Irregular Rhythm Notification and ECG app
deployment context: United Kingdom
sample: 264 patients at Mayo Clinic sites, of whom 41 had an explicit alert documented.
use-case relevant outcome: her pulse exceeded 120 beats per minute while she was inactive
what the sources leave unknown: No study in the sources separates the watch's part in long-term health from that of clinical care in these cases. In the Mayo Clinic study, only 11.4% of 264 patients seen after an abnormal pulse on an Apple Watch received an actionable cardiovascular diagnosis. The Italian study pooled four brands.

benefit: Medicare contractors cover Envisia to spare patients lung surgery
AI tool: Envisia Genomic Classifier
deployment context: Pulmonologists who order the test for Medicare patients with suspected idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis in the four contractors' jurisdictions; United States (the Medicare jurisdictions of Palmetto GBA, CGS, Noridian and WPS)
use-case relevant outcome: the same IPF or non-IPF diagnosis with the classifier as with histopathology in 92% of cases
what the sources leave unknown: No cited study shows better patient outcomes. The contractors only expect them from forthcoming studies. The 92% agreement comes from an interim analysis of 56 patients. The blinded test set held 49 patients, and sensitivity was 70% with an interval of 47% to 87%. The contractors rate the evidence limited in strength and weight.

benefit: FluChip-8G read by neural networks matched a cleared influenza test
AI tool: FluChip-8G Influenza A+B Assay
deployment context: InDevR (clinical study at three US testing sites on archived surveillance swabs); United States
use-case relevant outcome: sensitivity was 87.9% for influenza A and 100.0% for influenza B
what the sources leave unknown: Performance rests on frozen archived swabs tested against a cleared molecular assay. The study had 58 influenza A positives and 22 influenza B positives. Non-seasonal influenza A was assessed only on contrived samples. The FDA summary says that performance may vary with other emerging seasonal influenza A viruses.

benefit: Caption Guidance let nurses take usable heart scans
developer or vendor: Caption Health, Inc. (listed as Bay Labs, Inc. in the FDA database)
AI tool: Caption Guidance
deployment context: Northwestern Memorial Hospital and Minneapolis Heart Institute; Chicago, Illinois, and Minneapolis, Minnesota, United States
sample: Eight nurses, 240 patients, two US academic centers.
use-case relevant outcome: left ventricular size in 98.8% of exams
what the sources leave unknown: The Caption Guidance study had eight nurses and 240 patients, which the authors call small for judging generalizability. Patients were not recruited consecutively and none came from intensive care or the emergency department. There was no control group of nurses scanning without the software. Both sites were large academic hospitals. Caption Health funded the study and helped design and run it.

benefit: GI Genius helped endoscopists find more adenomas in a randomized trial
AI tool: GI Genius
deployment context: Humanitas Research Hospital, Nuovo Regina Margherita Hospital and Valduce Hospital (AID trial); Milan, Rome and Como, Italy
sample: 700 patients at three Italian hospitals, 263 low-risk patients in the FDA analysis and six endoscopists.
use-case relevant outcome: an adenoma detection rate of 55.1% with GI Genius against 42.0% with standard colonoscopy
what the sources leave unknown: The GI Genius trial measured adenoma detection, not cancer rates or deaths. Only six endoscopists in Italy took part. Race and ethnicity were not recorded, and FDA judged that the limited diversity likely made performance look overly optimistic. A Spanish health technology review noted that both trials came from a single author and report conflicts of interest.

benefit: Computer-read chest X-rays speed TB treatment at a Malawi clinic
AI tool: CAD4TB computer-aided detection software reading digital chest X-rays
deployment context: PROSPECT trial team of the Malawi-Liverpool-Wellcome Trust Clinical Research Programme at Bangwe Health Centre; Bangwe Health Centre, Blantyre, Malawi
sample: Bangwe Health Centre, Blantyre, Malawi, where 1,462 adults with cough were randomized 1:1:1 between 15 November 2018 and 27 November 2019.
use-case relevant outcome: Median time to treatment was 1 day in the X-ray arm and 11 days under standard care
what the sources leave unknown: TB was rarer than expected, so few people started treatment and the estimates are imprecise. Follow-up was short. The trial was open, with no blinding of participants or staff. The X-ray arm differed significantly only from standard care, not from HIV testing alone. Malawi's high HIV testing coverage may limit how far the findings apply elsewhere.

benefit: DEEPVESSEL FFR judged better than CT angiography in China's review
developer or vendor: Keya Medical, with 北京昆仑医云科技有限公司 (Beijing Kunlun Medical Cloud Technology Co., Ltd.) as the applicant in China
AI tool: DEEPVESSEL FFR (冠脉血流储备分数计算软件)
deployment context: 北京昆仑医云科技有限公司 (Beijing Kunlun Medical Cloud Technology Co., Ltd.), the applicant (prospective trial at three institutions and retrospective trial at six); Trial institutions in China that the report does not name, three in the prospective trial and six in the retrospective trial
what the sources leave unknown: CMDE's report gives no numbers from the two trials. The maker ran both, and both compared the software with invasive FFR in the same patients, one retrospectively. Their endpoints were diagnostic accuracy, not angiography or intervention avoided. Clinical evidence was lacking for patients with prior heart attack, stents, pacemakers or bypass grafts. CMDE said long-term safety and effectiveness still need follow-up.

benefit: DBLG1 closed loop kept glucose in range longer in a French trial
AI tool: DBLG1 System
deployment context: 12 French diabetes centers in the SP7 randomized crossover trial; France (12 trial centers)
use-case relevant outcome: 68.5% of the time in the target glucose range against 59.4%
what the sources leave unknown: SP7 was open-label and lasted 12 weeks per period. Trial patients had 48 hours of hospital training and round-the-clock support from a nurse and an engineer. The trial used a Dexcom G5 sensor and, at first, a Cellnovo pump, not the assessed system's G6 and Kaleido. HAS described the benefit on complications, HbA1c and quality of life as expected.

benefit: Apple Watch shows a woman's heart rate falling as her arrhythmia ends
AI tool: Apple Watch Series 3 heart-rate readings (optical photoplethysmography)
deployment context: Melbourne, Australia
use-case relevant outcome: a sudden drop in heart rate from 99 to 65 beats per minute at 19:29
what the sources leave unknown: The patient noticed the displayed heart rate herself. The sources show no machine-learning classifier, automatic alert, change in treatment or gain in health caused by AI.

benefit: Lunit INSIGHT CXR flags 13 resectable lung cancers on routine X-rays
AI tool: Lunit INSIGHT CXR
deployment context: Yongin Severance Hospital, Yonsei University College of Medicine; Yongin, South Korea
sample: 75 patients with surgically resected lung cancer at Yongin Severance Hospital from March 2020 to February 2022, of whom 13 had cancers found incidentally on radiographs taken for other reasons.
use-case relevant outcome: 13 (17.3%) had cancers found incidentally because the software flagged a nodule
what the sources leave unknown: In most cases, the authors cannot tell whether clinicians acted on the AI or on the radiologists' reports. The timing in the text and in Table 1 also disagree. Detection and resection do not show that survival improved.

benefit: Google software grades Thai diabetic eye photos as well as specialists
AI tool: Google Health deep-learning diabetic retinopathy screening system
deployment context: Thailand national diabetic retinopathy screening program (Ministry of Public Health guidelines) with Rajavithi Hospital, Bangkok; Thailand (nine primary-care sites)
use-case relevant outcome: For vision-threatening retinopathy the system's accuracy was 94.7%
what the sources leave unknown: Diagnostic accuracy and referral counts do not measure vision preserved, and the sources show no outcomes for the vision of the referred patients. Referrals also included ungradable images and low acuity. The plan to screen about 1 million people in Thailand over a decade is an announcement. The figure of more than one million patients screened comes from the makers' own comment and a summary of it.

benefit: Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid matched specialists when it gave a result
AI tool: Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid
deployment context: Fourteen US sites in the Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid validation study; Fourteen sites, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The Cognoa ASD Diagnosis Aid gave no result for 68 percent of the 425 children, so its accuracy figures cover 135 children. The study had a single arm and clinicians never saw the output, so no effect on care was measured. About a quarter of enrolled children dropped out. Five authors are Cognoa employees. New York's reviewers found no cost or cost-effectiveness studies.

benefit: Doctors treat a rhythm disorder after Galaxy Fit records a fast pulse
AI tool: Samsung Galaxy Fit heart-rate monitor and Galaxy Watch ECG app
deployment context: South Korea
use-case relevant outcome: recorded a peak resting pulse rate of 188 beats per minute
what the sources leave unknown: The wearables recorded the pulse or an ECG, and clinicians diagnosed and treated the arrhythmias. Samsung has not shown that the Galaxy Fit uses a learned model. No study in the sources separates the device's part from ordinary signal processing and the diagnostic ECG.

benefit: AIDRscreening met its targets for retinopathy in China's review
developer or vendor: Shenzhen SiBionics Intelligent Technology Co., Ltd. (深圳硅基智能科技有限公司)
AI tool: AIDRscreening (糖尿病视网膜病变眼底图像辅助诊断软件)
deployment context: Shenzhen SiBionics Intelligent Technology (prospective multicenter and retrospective registration trials); Trial centers that the report does not name, for a registration in China
what the sources leave unknown: The trials were the maker's own. The prospective multicenter trial had a single arm, with senior doctors' readings as the gold standard, and CMDE's report says only that the accuracy measures reached their targets, with no figures and no results for the secondary endpoints on time and daily diagnoses. No use after approval is reported.

benefit: Airdoc-AIFUNDUS met its targets for retinopathy in China's review
developer or vendor: Shanghai Airdoc Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (上海鹰瞳医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: Airdoc-AIFUNDUS (糖尿病视网膜病变眼底图像辅助诊断软件)
deployment context: Shanghai Airdoc Medical Technology (prospective multicenter registration trial); Trial sites in China that the report does not name
what the sources leave unknown: The maker ran a single-arm trial, and CMDE reports only that sensitivity and specificity reached their preset targets. It gives no figures, sites or patient numbers. CMDE says long-term safety and effectiveness still need tracking. It asked for more study of referral accuracy, including in primary care.

benefit: Fitbit Charge 3 signals precede 4 of 5 COVID-19 exacerbations
developer or vendor: Fitbit (device and EOV algorithm); Kanazawa University investigators (signal definitions)
AI tool: Fitbit Charge 3 estimated oxygen variation (EOV) and resting heart rate, with investigator-defined signal thresholds
deployment context: Kanazawa University and JCHO Kanazawa Hospital (DEXTERITY pilot, UMIN000041421); Kanazawa, Japan
sample: 23 patients with PCR-confirmed COVID-19 at JCHO Kanazawa Hospital, August to November 2020, with five exacerbation cases analyzed.
use-case relevant outcome: EOV signals preceded four of five analyzed cases (sensitivity 80%, specificity 90%)
what the sources leave unknown: The prediction rule was assessed after outcomes were known and did not trigger live treatment. The small analyzed subset limits the accuracy estimate, and the sources do not show that the device's oxygen estimation uses machine learning.

benefit: Confirmed TREWS sepsis alerts are linked to 3.3% lower mortality
AI tool: TREWS (Targeted Real-time Early Warning System)
deployment context: Johns Hopkins Medicine (five hospitals); Baltimore, United States
sample: Five Johns Hopkins hospitals, 2018 to September 2020, with 590,736 encounters monitored and 6,877 sepsis encounters analyzed (4,220 confirmed within 3 hours, 2,657 not).
what the sources leave unknown: When providers confirmed TREWS alerts sooner, mortality was lower in a selected cohort of patients with sepsis. How quickly clinicians respond, and how patients differ, may influence both confirmation and outcomes. The adjustment cannot show how much mortality fell because of the system itself.

benefit: X100 with Full Field PBS matched manual microscopy on 645 smears
AI tool: X100 with Full Field Peripheral Blood Smear Application
deployment context: Scopio Labs (method comparison against manual microscopy at three sites)
use-case relevant outcome: matched manual microscopy on 645 specimens, with 96.29% agreement
what the sources leave unknown: The study compared examiner-reviewed results with manual microscopy at three sites. Because examiners could change the network's classes, it does not isolate the network's own accuracy. It measured no time saved and no effect on diagnosis or treatment.

benefit: CoronaryDoc met its targets for triage of stenosis in China's review
developer or vendor: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology Co., Ltd. (语坤（北京）网络科技有限公司)
AI tool: CoronaryDoc (冠脉CT造影图像血管狭窄辅助分诊软件)
deployment context: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology (retrospective blinded registration trial at three institutions); Three qualified medical institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was retrospective and used three institutions, with manual reading as the gold standard. The report states only that the sensitivity and specificity targets were reached and gives no figures. CMDE requires more study of how the algorithm generalizes after approval and a yearly review of clinical use.

benefit: MIDS-PNAS aided the detection of lung nodules on CT in China's review
developer or vendor: Deepwise (杭州深睿博联科技有限公司)
AI tool: MIDS-PNAS (肺结节CT影像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Deepwise (prospective randomized crossover registration trial); Qualified medical institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
what the sources leave unknown: The report gives no figures for sensitivity, specificity or reading time, and the trial was the maker's own. The reference standard was a consensus reading by three senior chest radiologists. CMDE wrote that long-term safety and effectiveness still need tracking and asked for further study of how the algorithm generalizes.

benefit: Zio XT patch catches more heart rhythm problems than a 24-hour Holter
AI tool: Zio XT (Zio biosensor with ZEUS deep neural network ECG analysis)
deployment context: NHS organizations in England, with studies that included UK NHS sites; England, United Kingdom (guidance), with studies in the United Kingdom and United States
use-case relevant outcome: In three of four comparative studies, the yield over total wear time was higher
what the sources leave unknown: The four comparative studies had 357 people in all, too varied for a meta-analysis. In the UK trial, 20% refused the Holter monitor, and the assessors judged it likely underpowered. No study clearly defined accuracy against standard care, and the company's accuracy data were per episode, not per patient. No evidence shows that the higher yield improves clinical outcomes.

benefit: A brain–spine interface restored control of walking after paralysis
developer or vendor: NeuroRestore (EPFL/CHUV/UNIL) with CEA-Clinatec and ONWARD Medical
AI tool: STIMO-BSI brain–spine interface
deployment context: Lausanne University Hospital (CHUV); Lausanne, Switzerland
sample: One 38-year-old man at CHUV in Lausanne, ten years after an incomplete C5/C6 spinal cord injury.
use-case relevant outcome: walk more than 10 meters with crutches while the stimulation was off
what the sources leave unknown: The team reported on one man in Nature. ONWARD has counted later implants but has not said how many recipients recovered movement. No independent study is among the sources.

benefit: BoneView helps Poitiers emergency doctors read fracture X-rays
AI tool: BoneView
deployment context: Poitiers University Hospital (CHU de Poitiers); Emergency department, Poitiers University Hospital, Poitiers, France
sample: 3,720 adult trauma patients with limb radiographs (1,780 in 2020, 1,940 in 2021) at one level I trauma center.
use-case relevant outcome: the rate of discrepancies between emergency physicians' and radiologists' readings fell by 17%
what the sources leave unknown: The study is a retrospective before-and-after comparison at one hospital. The authors note that other, uncontrolled changes could explain the shorter stay. The change in clinically relevant discrepancies was not significant. Consultation counts came from medical reports that likely missed informal calls. The authors did not assess the software's financial impact.

benefit: INESSS finds AI retinopathy screening cheaper per correct result
AI tool: AI diabetic retinopathy screening systems (IARD) in the two economic studies, EyeArt and Retmarker in the UK and SELENA+ in Singapore
deployment context: Diabetic retinopathy screening programs in the United Kingdom and Singapore, as modeled in the studies that INESSS reviewed; United Kingdom and Singapore (studies), with guidance for Québec, Canada
what the sources leave unknown: INESSS found only two economic studies that compared screening with and without AI, from the UK and Singapore. It calls the cost section of the Singapore study very opaque, an important limit. It says that evidence of benefits is limited and highly uncertain for Québec. Québec has no established screening program, and its sensitivity, specificity and prices could differ.

benefit: QCovid adds 1.7 million people to England's shielding list
developer or vendor: Researchers led from the University of Oxford, using the QResearch database of general practice records
AI tool: QCovid risk stratification tool
deployment context: NHS England with NHS Digital, which kept the Shielded Patient List in England; England, United Kingdom
use-case relevant outcome: 1.7 million more people on England's Shielded Patient List
what the sources leave unknown: The UK Covid-19 Inquiry counts the people added to England's Shielded Patient List but reports no outcomes for them. Professor Whitty said there was an absence of evidence either way on whether shielding worked. Ethnicity was missing for 14% of those added, and missing values got high-risk defaults. The QCOVID developers validated the model on 2020 data and warned that absolute risks change over time.

benefit: AHI flagged unstable circulation from a single ECG lead
AI tool: Analytic for Hemodynamic Instability (AHI)
deployment context: Fifth Eye (prospective observational study at the University of Michigan Medical Center); Ann Arbor, Michigan, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The study was single-center and observational. It enrolled only patients with arterial lines, who were sicker than the intended population, so FDA calls results for telemetry patients uncertain. FDA expects, but the study did not show, better patient outcomes.

benefit: Insulin pump cuts low blood sugar for a mother who gives birth at term
AI tool: Medtronic MiniMed sensor-augmented pump / automated insulin delivery with predictive low glucose suspend (SmartGuard)
deployment context: not in the sources
sample: 22 women with type 1 diabetes who delivered between 2011 and 2021 at two Tokyo hospitals, of whom 11 used the MiniMed 640G with predictive low glucose suspend.
use-case relevant outcome: hypoglycemic episodes fell from 2.1–2.5 to 1.4 per day
what the sources leave unknown: The authors give no dates for the events. Fewer episodes of hypoglycemia and a live birth after two miscarriages do not show that the suspension of insulin caused the birth. The study of 2024 in Tokyo and the case of 2025 with the MiniMed 780G concern other patients.

benefit: Yitu_AICare_Bone_Age kept errors within its target in China's review
developer or vendor: Hangzhou Yitu Healthcare Technology Co., Ltd. (杭州依图医疗技术有限公司)
AI tool: Yitu_AICare_Bone_Age (儿童手部X射线影像骨龄辅助评估软件)
deployment context: Hangzhou Yitu Healthcare Technology (prospective registration trial with 1,000 subjects at four institutions); Four clinical institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
what the sources leave unknown: The maker's trial was single-arm and compared the software with an expert panel against a preset target, and the report gives no error figures. The trial did not measure reading time. Few subjects aged 0.5 to 6 or 13 to 18 took part, and the algorithm work drew mainly on Han Chinese people.

benefit: WHO recommends AI reading of chest X-rays for TB screening
developer or vendor: Delft Imaging (CAD4TB), Lunit (Lunit INSIGHT CXR) and Qure.ai (qXR)
AI tool: CAD4TB, Lunit INSIGHT CXR and qXR (computer-aided detection software for TB)
deployment context: TB screening and triage studies in three independent evaluations reviewed by WHO; Global
what the sources leave unknown: WHO could not pool the accuracy estimates across the three CAD programs or their evaluations. Accuracy varied substantially across settings, even for one program at one threshold. The recommendation is conditional, rests on low-certainty evidence and covers only bacteriologically confirmed TB. In screening populations, the software's specificity of 0.23 to 0.66 fell below WHO's target of more than 0.70.

benefit: Oxehealth Vital Signs read two vital signs from a camera in the room
AI tool: Oxehealth Vital Signs
deployment context: Oxehealth (clinical accuracy study in 60 adults against a contact device)
what the sources leave unknown: The study FDA reviewed was observational and uncontrolled, with 60 adults, and was not powered for subgroups. It measured accuracy against a contact device only. Within the label, 58% of attempts gave a pulse rate and 73% a breathing rate. The subject must be still. No count of room entries avoided or harms to staff or patients is reported.

benefit: Gili Pro BioSensor measured two vital signs without contact
AI tool: Gili Pro BioSensor (Gili BioSensor System)
deployment context: ContinUse Biometrics (clinical accuracy study in 120 adults against ECG and capnography)
what the sources leave unknown: The study was the sponsor's, and clinical testing covered only 38 to 100 beats and 6 to 34 breaths per minute. The device is for adult spot checks with the patient seated and in smooth, snug clothing. The summary says that remote readings can reduce staff exposure to infection but reports no data on exposure. It includes no patient perspectives.

benefit: HeartFlow FFRCT may spare heart patients invasive tests, NICE finds
AI tool: HeartFlow FFRCT
deployment context: NHS services in England that offer coronary CT angiography, with the NXT and PLATFORM study sites in NICE's evidence; England, United Kingdom (guidance), with studies in several countries
use-case relevant outcome: 12% in that arm had no obstructive disease at angiography, against 73%
what the sources leave unknown: The recommendation covers only patients with stable, recent-onset chest pain who are offered CT angiography, and it requires 64-slice or better facilities. NICE writes that the test may avoid invasive angiography and revascularisation, and that savings of £391 per patient may follow, assuming access to appropriate facilities.

benefit: Model-chosen calls keep more Indian mothers listening to health messages
developer or vendor: Google and Harvard University (Milind Tambe's group) with ARMMAN
AI tool: mMitra’s service-call scheduler, using a restless multi-armed bandit policy with clustered transition estimates and a random forest
deployment context: ARMMAN; India (ARMMAN mMitra program areas)
sample: The groups contained 7,668, 7,668, and 7,667 participants, respectively.
use-case relevant outcome: reduced cumulative engagement drops by 32.0% compared with messaging alone
what the sources leave unknown: The trial measured weekly listening and did not measure clinical health. Every cited source comes from the developers and ARMMAN, and none is independent.

benefit: Smart wristwatch prompts a patient's return to hospital for an embolism
developer or vendor: Not stated (the abstract does not name the device's maker)
AI tool: Smart wristwatch / personal activity monitor (brand, model and alert type not stated in the abstract)
deployment context: Toronto, Canada (authors' institution; the abstract does not state where the case occurred)
what the sources leave unknown: Only the abstract is available. It reports one patient, with no age, sex, operation or outcome given. It does not say what the wristwatch measured or what it alerted on, and it does not name the device. There is no comparison and no follow-up.

benefit: Cybersight AI results on the day lift eye referrals in Kigali
AI tool: Cybersight AI
deployment context: Orbis International with the Rwanda International Institute of Ophthalmology, at four diabetes clinics; Kigali, Rwanda
sample: 275 adults with referable findings at four diabetes clinics in and around Kigali, March to July 2021.
use-case relevant outcome: raised 30-day referral attendance to 51.5% from 39.6% with delayed human grading
what the sources leave unknown: The trial measured referral attendance within 30 days, not vision outcomes. The difference had P = 0.048. It compared immediate AI results with delayed human grading, so the effect cannot be separated from the speed of the result. The sample was 60% urban, and the AI had not been validated in peer-reviewed work for people of African descent. Orbis employees were among the authors.

benefit: Mayo Clinic's AI-ECG flags a weakly pumping heart in a man who recovers
developer or vendor: Mayo Clinic (licensed to Eko and Anumana)
AI tool: Mayo Clinic AI-ECG low-ejection-fraction algorithm (AI-ECG dashboard)
deployment context: Mayo Clinic, Rochester; Rochester, Minnesota, USA
use-case relevant outcome: at four months his ejection fraction had improved to 55%
what the sources leave unknown: The patient's recovery followed treatment, possible recovery from a virus and weight loss. The developers, who wrote the case report, cannot separate those effects or show the outcome without AI. The probability score is not a measured benefit of treatment.

benefit: Scotland backs HeartFlow FFRCT as an option to avoid invasive tests
AI tool: HeartFlow FFRCT
deployment context: NHSScotland health boards, with a pilot at NHS Western Isles from December 2020; Scotland, United Kingdom
what the sources leave unknown: SHTG's council judged the evidence that HeartFlow FFRCT reduces invasive angiography to be limited, resting on non-randomized and post hoc studies. The size of any cost saving is uncertain because Scottish practice in investigating chest pain varies. Scottish experts said that the NICE cost model's assumptions, such as decisions hinging on an FFR below 0.80, do not reflect practice.

benefit: Paige Prostate helped pathologists catch cancer missed on a first read
AI tool: Paige Prostate
deployment context: Paige.AI (pivotal reader study with sixteen pathologists); United States
sample: Sixteen pathologists, 610 whole slide images originally and 171 cancer slides analyzed for the sensitivity change.
use-case relevant outcome: improvement in sensitivity in 7.3% of biopsy images
what the sources leave unknown: Sixteen pathologists classified slides for the study without immunohistochemistry stains, and their reads did not guide care. Each assisted read came directly after an unassisted read of the same image. All slides were scanned on one scanner unit. FDA notes that the 7.3% gain is per biopsy and would likely be substantially lower per patient.

benefit: Doctors treat ventricular tachycardia after Fitbit flags a fast heart
AI tool: Fitbit Sense ECG app and heart-rate monitoring
deployment context: Jamshedpur, India
use-case relevant outcome: detected an irregular heart rate of 164 beats per minute with irregular rhythm
what the sources leave unknown: The man had symptoms as well as the watch reading, so the watch's part cannot be separated from that of his symptoms. The app's clearance covers only the detection of atrial fibrillation or sinus rhythm, and ventricular tachycardia lies outside it.

benefit: Dxcover blood test separated patients by whether they had brain cancer
AI tool: Dxcover brain cancer liquid biopsy test
deployment context: Brain tumor early diagnosis study in NHS Lothian at the Western General Hospital, Edinburgh (patients referred for direct-access CT and patients with new brain tumors); Edinburgh, Scotland, United Kingdom
what the sources leave unknown: The published study came from one center in secondary care. SHTG notes that the cohort was enriched with patients with known brain cancer and held only three cancers among the patients referred from primary care, so it did not match the primary care population for which the Dxcover test is meant. SHTG states that firm conclusions cannot be drawn without evaluation in general practice.

benefit: Medicare credits Guardian implants with faster care in heart attacks
AI tool: AngelMed Guardian System
deployment context: Sites of the ALERTS trial in the United States, which the documents do not name; United States
use-case relevant outcome: 51 minutes with alarms on and 30.6 hours with alarms off
what the sources leave unknown: The trial's composite primary endpoint was not statistically significant. Events were fewer than expected, and the trial stopped early. Patients knew whether their alarms were on. The 1.7-hour and 8.0-hour figures come from a later retrospective analysis that added data from outside the randomized period. In 2016 an FDA panel voted 12–0 that effectiveness was not reasonably assured.

benefit: Faculty's bed tool for Kettering goes open source without being deployed
developer or vendor: Faculty (applied AI company) with NHS AI Lab Skunkworks (NHSX) and Kettering General Hospital, through the Home Office Accelerated Capability Environment
AI tool: NHS AI Lab Skunkworks bed-allocation proof of concept (Bayesian demand forecasting with greedy and Monte Carlo tree search allocation agents and a web user interface)
deployment context: Kettering General Hospital NHS Foundation Trust (proof-of-concept testing only); Kettering, Northamptonshire, England
what the sources leave unknown: No live deployment, measured improvement in allocation, change in waiting times or patient benefit is documented. Only the greedy agent reached the interface. Tree search had performance problems, and reinforcement learning was not developed. Accounts of the project's length differ, at 12 and 14 weeks.

benefit: CAD4TB helps screen 94,694 people in Nigeria, of whom 2,337 have TB
AI tool: CAD4TB computer-aided detection on ultra-portable digital chest X-ray
deployment context: KNCV Tuberculosis Foundation Nigeria and Institute of Human Virology Nigeria with the National TB and Leprosy Control Program, funded by USAID; Eight states, Nigeria
what the sources leave unknown: The text and the tables of the study disagree on the number of TB diagnoses. Symptom screening also triggered testing, and 723 of the people diagnosed fell below the AI threshold. Because populations and access to the program differ, CAD4TB cannot be credited with all the extra diagnoses or treatment starts.

benefit: Doctors find lung cancer after a smartwatch flags a fast heart rate
developer or vendor: Not stated (the report does not name the device's maker)
AI tool: Smartwatch heart-rate and irregular-rhythm alert (brand and model not stated)
deployment context: United Kingdom (authors at St George's Healthcare NHS Trust, London, and East Surrey Hospital, Redhill; the treating hospitals are not named)
use-case relevant outcome: The 35 mm tumor was staged pT2a pN0 M0 with clear margins
what the sources leave unknown: The watch's brand and algorithm are unspecified, so whether AI was involved remains open. The lung cancer was found on a chest X-ray after the procedure, and the watch did not detect it. The claim that surgery would otherwise have become impossible is a conjecture with no follow-up evidence.

benefit: Face2Gene lists a rare disorder that sequencing confirms after 18 years
AI tool: Face2Gene (DeepGestalt facial phenotyping)
deployment context: Department of Neurology, National Hospital Organization Akita National Hospital; Yurihonjo, Japan
what the sources leave unknown: Face2Gene introduced several candidate diagnoses after clinical doubt had already arisen. Sequencing established the DYRK1A diagnosis. The sources do not show that AI alone corrected the diagnosis, and the Akita team reports no measure of time saved and no better treatment or function.

benefit: nodoca throat photos met preset goals for accuracy in Japan's review
developer or vendor: Aillis, Inc. (アイリス株式会社)
AI tool: nodoca (ノドカ)
deployment context: Aillis (trial at 11 sites in Japan, with the approved version run on stored trial data); Japan (11 trial sites)
what the sources leave unknown: The approved nodoca was not tested on new patients. Aillis, the maker, re-ran it on stored data from its earlier device's open-label trial after removing 13 patients whose data could not be analyzed. Sensitivity was not shown non-inferior to the rapid antigen test. PMDA notes that the device does not detect the virus directly.

benefit: Model Dermatology helps trainees diagnose skin lesions in Seoul
developer or vendor: Seung Seog Han (I Dermatology Clinic and IDerma, Inc.)
AI tool: Model Dermatology
deployment context: Department of Dermatology, Asan Medical Center, Ulsan University College of Medicine; Seoul, South Korea
sample: 576 consecutive adults with suspicious skin lesions at a tertiary hospital in Seoul. Eight non-expert physicians.
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was single-center and unmasked, at one Seoul hospital. Han, who develops and maintains Model Dermatology, is its first author. The 576 patients had skin types III or IV. The endpoint was diagnostic accuracy, not any patient outcome. The gain for dermatology residents was not significant.

benefit: Mayo credits AI with finding a woman's ruptured brain aneurysm fast
AI tool: AI analysis of brain CT images
deployment context: Mayo Clinic; Jacksonville, Florida, United States
what the sources leave unknown: Mayo does not name the software or compare her care with care without it, and it gives no measure of her treatment time.

benefit: Viz.ai stroke alerts shortened thrombectomy start times in Houston
AI tool: Viz.ai automated large vessel occlusion detection with mobile alerting (Viz LVO)
deployment context: UTHealth Houston stroke program at four comprehensive stroke centers in greater Houston; Four comprehensive stroke centers in the greater Houston area, Texas, United States
sample: 243 patients with large vessel occlusion treated with thrombectomy at four Houston comprehensive stroke centers.
what the sources leave unknown: All four centers belonged to one health system with shared workflows, and some physicians worked at several of them. Staff knew when the alerts were active. The trial was too small to detect differences in clinical outcomes. An independent review rated its randomization as raising some concerns. The senior author received grants from Viz.ai during the study.

benefit: Doctors find vasculitis after Fitbit shows a rising resting heart rate
AI tool: Fitbit Alta HR resting heart rate (Fitbit app)
deployment context: Zurich, Switzerland
use-case relevant outcome: resting heart rate had risen persistently from about 55 to about 75 beats per minute
what the sources leave unknown: The patient noticed the trend, and clinicians did the diagnostic work. A reading from a smartwatch is not enough to show that an AI inference caused the benefit. One case cannot show that such screening works.

benefit: uAI-HematomaCare flagged brain bleeds on CT in China's review
developer or vendor: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence Co., Ltd. (上海联影智能医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: uAI-HematomaCare (颅内出血CT影像辅助分诊软件)
deployment context: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence (retrospective registration trial on head CT of 600 subjects from three centers); Three centers that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: a sensitivity of 97.32% and a specificity of 99.67%
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence's own. It was retrospective and single-arm, on stored scans from three centers, with senior doctors' readings as the reference. It measured sensitivity and specificity only. Screening time was not measured, so the gain in efficiency is CMDE's judgment. No result from use after approval is reported.

benefit: Xuanwu Hospital implants China's first responsive neurostimulator
developer or vendor: Hangzhou Genlight MedTech Co. Ltd. (GenLight MedTech), identified in the later clinical-team publication.
AI tool: Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system (brain-computer interface)
deployment context: Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing; Beijing, China
sample: 10 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy at Xuanwu Hospital (3), Second Affiliated Hospital of Zhejiang University (6) and Huashan Hospital (1), enrolled March to November 2022.
what the sources leave unknown: In its papers, the trial team reports a mean seizure reduction of 61.1% in seven patients and a median reduction of 58% at month 12 in 19 patients. The team gives no outcome for this first patient in either paper, and neither paper shows that a learned model predicted seizures.

benefit: Athelas Home let patients run white-cell counts at home
AI tool: Athelas Home
deployment context: Athelas (at-home study in which 61 patients or their caregivers ran the tests)
what the sources leave unknown: The home results were compared with the maker's own predicate device, Athelas One, run by trained operators. The study had 61 patients and reported no clinical outcomes. Flagging was tested on Athelas One, not on the home device.

benefit: In a Taiwan trial, fewer patients died when AI picked out high-risk ECGs
developer or vendor: National Defense Medical Center and Tri-Service General Hospital research team
AI tool: AI-ECG mortality prediction and physician alert system
deployment context: An academic medical center and a community hospital in Taiwan; Taiwan
sample: The analysis included 15,965 adults treated by 39 physicians at two hospitals in Taiwan.
what the sources leave unknown: The deployed model weights, longer-term survival and the clinical actions that caused the mortality difference remain unknown.

benefit: A VA trial ties STORM case reviews to lower odds of death
AI tool: STORM (Stratification Tool for Opioid Risk Mitigation)
deployment context: Veterans Health Administration, all 140 medical centers; United States (all 140 VHA medical centers)
use-case relevant outcome: 22% lower odds of death within four months
what the sources leave unknown: Mortality was an exploratory outcome, and the nine primary serious adverse events showed no detectable effect. Unadjusted death rates were 6.7% without the mandate and 6.9% with it, and only the adjusted model gives lower odds. Outcomes were censored at 127 days, and adverse events were captured only when patients used VHA facilities.

benefit: After a RapidAI stroke alert, doctors reopen a firefighter's artery fast
AI tool: RapidAI imaging platform (automated LVO detection)
deployment context: Memorial Healthcare System / Memorial Neuroscience Institute (Memorial Hospital West); Memorial Hospital West, United States
use-case relevant outcome: restored flow under 60 minutes from arrival
what the sources leave unknown: The hospital reports rapid reperfusion and the patient's lack of deficits. It does not separate the time saved by RapidAI from the pre-notification, the imaging, the staffing and the thrombectomy. One success cannot show how many similar patients the system helps.

benefit: Insight MMG as a third reader finds more breast cancers in Stockholm
AI tool: Lunit INSIGHT MMG
deployment context: Capio Sankt Göran Hospital with Karolinska Institutet (ScreenTrustCAD study); Stockholm, Sweden
sample: 55,581 women aged 40 to 74 screened at Capio Sankt Göran Hospital, 1 April 2021 to 9 June 2022.
use-case relevant outcome: the three together found 269 cancers against 250 by the radiologists alone
what the sources leave unknown: The ScreenTrustCAD study was single-arm and paired, so it cannot compare interval cancer rates between reading strategies. Its planned 23-month follow-up had not yet been done. It ran at one hospital with one mammography vendor and one AI system, which limits generalisability. Lunit, the maker of Insight MMG, was one of the funders. No quality assurance protocol existed to detect data drift in the AI's performance.

benefit: Imagene AI predicts a mutation, letting treatment start in two days
AI tool: Imagene AI (H&E-based molecular inference)
deployment context: Tel Aviv Sourasky Medical Center; Tel Aviv, Israel
use-case relevant outcome: one week earlier than routine practice and avoided whole-neuraxis radiotherapy
what the sources leave unknown: The AI's prediction needed confirmation by PCR. The week gained is measured against routine practice, with no matched alternative. The later response cannot separate the AI's part from osimertinib and clinical care.

benefit: Minuteful - kidney test let lay users test their own urine albumin
AI tool: Minuteful - kidney test
deployment context: Healthy.io (method comparison with 466 lay users)
use-case relevant outcome: matched a trained operator's in 92.7% of cases
what the sources leave unknown: The 92.7% match is agreement with another urine test system, the URiSCAN Optima, used by a trained operator. Users tested with only two phone models in that study. The FDA summary reports no clinical sensitivity or specificity. The UK studies that SHTG reviewed were single-arm observational studies, and the predicted cost savings rest on assumptions that positive results are followed up.

benefit: EndoScreener lowered the rate of missed adenomas in China's review
developer or vendor: Chengdu Wision Medical Device Co., Ltd. (成都微识医疗设备有限公司, the applicant) and Shanghai Wision AI
AI tool: EndoScreener (肠息肉电子结肠内窥镜图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Chengdu Wision Medical Device (registration trial with 223 patients at four US academic medical centers); Four US academic medical centers (CMDE's report says only that they were outside China)
use-case relevant outcome: missed 20.12% of adenomas with EndoScreener, against 31.25% without it
what the sources leave unknown: The trial that the maker submitted included 223 patients at four institutions outside China. It was single-blind, and the same endoscopist did both exams for each patient. The gain in first-pass adenoma detection rate was not statistically significant. CMDE judged the device on the maker's submission before approval.

benefit: Pregnant women in Kenya learn more from a text-message health service
AI tool: PROMPTS, an SMS health platform with automated message classification and a clinical helpdesk; TRIM-AI was introduced in June 2022
deployment context: Jacaranda Health with Kenyan county health facilities; Eight counties (Kajiado, Kilifi, Kirinyaga, Kisii, Meru, Narok, Nyeri, Siaya), Kenya
sample: There were 6,139 participants at 40 facilities. Researchers completed 5,509 of 6,128 eligible postpartum interviews.
use-case relevant outcome: improvements of 0.06–0.09 standard deviations across five measures
what the sources leave unknown: The trial evaluated the whole platform, so it did not measure the separate effect of the natural-language processing helpdesk. The trial was not powered for clinical outcomes. The helpdesk system changed in June 2022, during follow-up.

benefit: No-show predictions guided reminder calls that cut missed visits
AI tool: Epic no-show prediction model (random forest), localized at MetroHealth
deployment context: MetroHealth; MetroHealth internal medicine primary care clinic, Cleveland, Ohio, United States
sample: 5,840 appointments with predicted no-show risk of 15% or higher at a MetroHealth internal medicine clinic.
use-case relevant outcome: the no-show rate was 33% with calls and 36% without
what the sources leave unknown: The MetroHealth initiative ran in one safety-net clinic, so its results may not generalize elsewhere. It did not account for socioeconomic status as a confounder for race. The authors could not identify why live calls worked better than automated reminders. The design allowed no formal cost analysis.

benefit: MY-YD-01 raised detection of glaucoma-like damage on fundus photos
developer or vendor: Tencent Healthcare (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. (腾讯医疗健康（深圳）有限公司)
AI tool: MY-YD-01 (慢性青光眼样视神经病变眼底图像辅助诊断软件)
deployment context: Tencent Healthcare (Shenzhen) (registration trial with 1,092 subjects at four institutions); Four trial institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
what the sources leave unknown: The evidence is Tencent's own pre-market trial, and CMDE judged it from the applicant's materials. The report does not say how the trial and control groups read the photographs. The subject-level sensitivity gain has a wide confidence interval, from 3.09% to 28.97%. The trial measured detection, not patients' outcomes.

benefit: iSciLab tests nose-print AI that registers animals to track vaccination
AI tool: iSciLab biometric animal-registration system
deployment context: iSciLab, testing with the South Korean government; South Korea and unspecified African field-test settings
what the sources leave unknown: The outcome of the two-year demonstration project, for which the Ministry of Science and ICT selected the AniPuppy app in September 2022, has not been reported. Neither have the outcomes of the horse-passport and African pilots. iSciLab gives no assessed reduction in rabies, identification fraud or invasive procedures in its submission, and the accuracy figures in the news reports come from the company.

benefit: Doctors find a pulmonary embolism after Apple Watch records low oxygen
AI tool: Apple Watch Blood Oxygen app
deployment context: Yufu, Oita Prefecture, Japan
use-case relevant outcome: Apple Watch Series 7 had shown an oxygen saturation of 88% in the early morning
what the sources leave unknown: This is a single clinical case, and clinicians made the diagnosis with computed tomography angiography. The authors do not describe how the watch's oxygen algorithm works, and they describe no automatic alert. They do not say who reported the reading. A systematic review of 2023 covered five studies of the Series 6 with 973 patients. Its authors found no strong systematic bias against medical-grade pulse oximeters, with outliers of up to 15 points.

benefit: Software flags a brain tumor while a woman is still in the scanner
developer or vendor: Gazi University, Ankara (Department of Neurosurgery and Department of Computer Engineering), within the Turkish Brain Project funded by the Presidency of the Republic of Türkiye, with the Presidency's Digital Transformation Office credited for the model's development
AI tool: Turkish Brain Project real-time brain MRI alert system at Gazi University: a region-based convolutional neural network object-detection algorithm integrated into the hospital network, which processes MRI images in real time; Anadolu Agency reports that it evaluates a brain MRI within 5-10 seconds while the patient is still in the scanner and sends the physicians' mobile phones a message with the abnormal regions segmented, through a GSM operator's picture-message service
deployment context: Gazi University, Department of Neurosurgery, Ankara; Ankara, Turkey
what the sources leave unknown: How long this patient would have waited without the alert is unknown. The developers report a prompt diagnosis, but they did not measure the effect of that timing on survival or other clinical outcomes.

benefit: CMD-1 cuts crisis triage from 9 hours to 8–13 minutes
developer or vendor: Cerebral Inc. with Stanford University School of Medicine collaborators
AI tool: CMD-1 (Crisis Message Detector 1): key-word filter followed by a logistic-regression classifier on chat messages
deployment context: Cerebral Inc.; United States
sample: 102,471 chat messages sent by 32,803 patients of Cerebral, a national United States tele-mental-health provider, from 1 to 31 October 2022.
use-case relevant outcome: the daily median time from message receipt to crisis-specialist triage was 8 to 13 minutes
what the sources leave unknown: The predeployment baseline is an internal historical comparison, so staffing and workflow changes are not controlled. The prospective labels, exclusions by the keyword filter, false negatives and uncertainty need examination. Faster triage does not establish fewer attempts, hospitalizations, or deaths.

benefit: On CT, PANDA detects pancreatic cancers that standard care missed
AI tool: PANDA deep-learning CT screening model
deployment context: Shanghai, China
sample: 3,208 training patients at one Shanghai center. A multicenter validation of 6,239 patients from 10 centers, including 5,337 patients from nine external centers in mainland China, Taiwan and the Czech Republic. 20,530 consecutive patients in the real-world test and 33 readers from 12 institutions in the first reader study.
what the sources leave unknown: The real-world test was retrospective. No survival gain has been reported. The authors of an independent 2026 review report that no study shows that the use of PANDA improves stage at diagnosis or survival.

benefit: GI Genius lifts adenoma detection in VA colonoscopy units
AI tool: GI Genius Intelligent Endoscopy Module
deployment context: Veterans Health Administration, National Gastroenterology and Hepatology Program; 42 VA medical facilities, United States
sample: 269 endoscopists at 42 equipped facilities and 547 at 97 control facilities, with 334,200 colonoscopies.
what the sources leave unknown: The VA study was a pragmatic quality improvement study that compared adenoma detection before and after deployment at randomly selected facilities. The authors state that the impact on cancer outcomes and on endoscopist deskilling remains undetermined. The review notes that the preventive value of computer-aided detection cannot be inferred from adenoma detection and that much of the added detection involves diminutive adenomas.

benefit: ScanNav Anatomy PNB helped anesthesiologists find the right view
AI tool: ScanNav Anatomy Peripheral Nerve Block
deployment context: Intelligent Ultrasound (study with 15 expert and 15 trainee anesthesiologists at Oregon Health & Science University); Portland, Oregon, United States
what the sources leave unknown: FDA states that the benefits were assessed subjectively, by questionnaire.
