Intelligent Ultrasound ran the study with 30 participants scanning two volunteers in a simulated clinical setting. No nerve block was performed, so effects on block success and complications are unknown. The submission included no information on patient perspectives.

benefit: JF CXR-1 agreed with expert readers on TB chest X-rays in a trial
developer or vendor: Jiangxi Zhongke Jiufeng Smart Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (江西中科九峰智慧医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: JF CXR-1 (肺结核X射线图像辅助评估软件)
deployment context: Jiangxi Zhongke Jiufeng Smart Medical Technology (prospective trial with 1,165 cases at six centers); Six trial centers in China that the report does not name
use-case relevant outcome: 94.19% of positive and 91.17% of negative chest X-rays
what the sources leave unknown: The evidence is the applicant's own pre-market trial, and its main reference was a reading panel rather than clinical diagnosis. After two weeks of follow-up, 29 subjects still had no diagnosis. CMDE said that long-term safety and effectiveness need tracking and asked for study of how well the algorithm generalizes.

benefit: Avive AED exceeded the goals of the AHA for spotting shockable rhythms
AI tool: Avive AED System rhythm recognition detector
deployment context: Avive Solutions (bench tests on a held-out set of ECG recordings)
what the sources leave unknown: The rhythm results come from the maker's own ECG test set, with one recording per person, and demographic information on the recordings is limited. Clinical evidence came from published studies of a similar Philips waveform, not from a study of the Avive AED. The AED had not been marketed anywhere when FDA approved it.

benefit: CellaScope helped lab staff identify white blood cells on smears
developer or vendor: Beijing Xiaoying Technology Co., Ltd. (北京小蝇科技有限责任公司)
AI tool: CellaScope (外周血细胞图像白细胞辅助识别软件)
deployment context: Beijing Xiaoying Technology (registration trial at Peking Union Medical College Hospital, the Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University and Dongyang People's Hospital); Beijing, Changsha (Hunan) and Dongyang (Zhejiang), China
use-case relevant outcome: 70.22% of abnormal white blood cells on smears with CellaScope, against 39.10% alone
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own, run before approval in 494 patients at three hospitals. Accuracy was judged against an expert panel's reading of the same smears, not against patient outcomes. The software may not serve alone as a basis for diagnosis or treatment. The report claims only better identification accuracy and gives no effect on care, time or workload.

benefit: FMF screening algorithm probably predicts preterm preeclampsia better
AI tool: Fetal Medicine Foundation (FMF) first-trimester preeclampsia screening algorithm (maternal characteristics, mean arterial pressure, uterine artery pulsatility index and PlGF)
deployment context: Screening studies in Asia and Europe that FHI pooled, with screening proposed for Norway's specialist health service; Studies in Asia and Europe, assessed for Norway
use-case relevant outcome: the sensitivity for preeclampsia before week 37 was 0.728
what the sources leave unknown: FHI found no systematic reviews and pooled 16 primary studies, half from Asia and half from Europe, none from Norway. Sensitivity before 34 weeks had low confidence. Studies in which no women took aspirin reported higher sensitivity than studies in which women did. Only one study covered aspirin's clinical effect. The cost model rests on uncertain assumptions, and FHI calls for an implementation study.

benefit: An AI eye exam increased screening among young people with diabetes
AI tool: IDx-DR (now LumineticsCore)
deployment context: Johns Hopkins Pediatric Diabetes Center; Baltimore, United States
sample: The trial randomized 164 participants at two Baltimore clinics. After one control was excluded, the analysis included 81 AI participants and 82 controls.
use-case relevant outcome: all 81 young people offered IDx-DR completed an eye exam, compared with 18 of 82 controls
what the sources leave unknown: The authors do not report later outcomes for vision or the exact software release, and they do not isolate the algorithm's own effect.

benefit: Fewer sepsis patients die after COMPOSER alerts UC San Diego nurses
developer or vendor: University of California San Diego research team
AI tool: COMPOSER deep-learning sepsis prediction and nurse alert system
deployment context: UC San Diego Health; San Diego, California, United States
sample: The analysis included 6,217 eligible sepsis encounters: 5,065 before deployment and 1,152 afterward.
what the sources leave unknown: The authors did not measure harms from false alarms in patients without sepsis or financial returns, and the sources include no independent replication of the mortality effect.

benefit: Transpara helps Swedish breast screening find more cancers
AI tool: Transpara
deployment context: Unilabs Mammography Unit at Skåne University Hospital with Lund University (MASAI trial, Swedish national screening program); Malmö, Lund, Landskrona and Trelleborg, Skåne, Sweden
sample: Study 1: 105,934 women screened at four sites in southwest Sweden, 12 April 2021 to 7 December 2022. Study 2: 105,915 women analyzed.
use-case relevant outcome: a detection rate of 6.4 per 1,000 against 5.0 per 1,000
what the sources leave unknown: A 2026 review notes that MASAI is the only randomized trial to have reported, from one country with one AI system. The radiologists knew which arm each examination was in. Race and ethnicity were not collected. The lower interval cancer rate was not statistically significant. Whether the extra cancers found mean fewer deaths or more overdiagnosis is still in follow-up.

benefit: EMA backs the iBox score to forecast kidney graft loss in trials
developer or vendor: Paris Transplant Group (INSERM UMR 970, AP-HP and University of Paris)
AI tool: iBox Scoring System (iBox prediction algorithm)
deployment context: C-Path's Transplant Therapeutics Consortium (validation for EMA) and the Paris Transplant Group (comparison with nine physicians); France (derivation data from four transplant centers), with validation in the United States, Finland and two international trials
what the sources leave unknown: EMA found too few completed randomized trials to validate iBox as a surrogate primary endpoint. AQuAS found only one study that compared iBox with physicians, with nine physicians and predictions at seven years only, no study of clinical or technical safety, and no published results from the ongoing trials. The group that built iBox ran that comparison on 400 past patients.

benefit: FOX fits cochlear implants at least as well as manual fitting in a trial
AI tool: FOX (Fitting to Outcome eXpert) / AI-FOX cochlear-implant fitting software
deployment context: Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels; Brussels, Belgium
sample: 24 patients receiving a first cochlear implant at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels, randomized to FOX or manual fitting for one year, then switched.
use-case relevant outcome: 100% of the manual group kept the FOX map and 82% performed better with it
what the sources leave unknown: The sources contain no assessment of the small crossover trial and the companion studies for allocation, carryover, missing results and the authors' ties to Otoconsult. Better speech scores did not mean that every patient found FOX more comfortable, and 63% of the FOX group preferred its manual map. Long-term everyday benefit is unmeasured here.

benefit: Software flags a severe artery blockage that a manual reading underrated
developer or vendor: China Medical University Hospital (中國醫藥大學附設醫院人工智慧中心), director 許凱程
AI tool: 運動心電圖AI輔助判讀系統 (Exercise ECG AI-Assisted Interpretation System), China Medical University Hospital
deployment context: China Medical University Hospital, Division of Cardiology (心臟血管系), Taichung; Taichung, Taiwan
use-case relevant outcome: a 99 percent stenosis of the left anterior descending artery
what the sources leave unknown: The figure of 72% is a probability of severe narrowing. It does not measure how much of the artery was blocked, and angiography found 99% stenosis. One case and the hospital's own statement of what would otherwise have happened are not enough to show that a death was prevented. In the later study of the model, the authors report a high rate of false positives.

benefit: A surgeon finds a tethered cord after ChatGPT narrows a mother's search
AI tool: ChatGPT
deployment context: Michigan, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The sources do not show how accurate ChatGPT is across patients or what would have happened without it. The mother said that ChatGPT gave three possible diagnoses and that stories from other parents on social media led her to tethered cord syndrome. The surgeon said that she found the tethered cord herself. The later recovery rests on the mother's statement that he is a new kid now.

benefit: qXR and Genki cut the cost of reading X-rays for TB in India
AI tool: qXR and Genki (AI-assisted chest X-ray interpretation for TB screening)
deployment context: Public health facilities in Chennai, Tamil Nadu (Genki) and Maharashtra (qXR) screening for TB under India's National Tuberculosis Elimination Program; Chennai, Tamil Nadu, and Maharashtra, India
use-case relevant outcome: INR 30 with qXR and INR 22 with Genki
what the sources leave unknown: The analysis took the provider's view and used no matched comparisons. Cost and program data came from the makers and secondary sources. Accuracy came from published studies, not from these sites. The radiologist's cost rests on an assumed 10% share of one salary, and the radiologist data date from 2021 to 2022, before the AI data of 2023.

benefit: AI-BAC helped doctors find more breast lesions on mammograms
developer or vendor: Deepwise (杭州深睿博联科技有限公司)
AI tool: AI-BAC (乳腺X射线图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Deepwise (randomized crossover reader trial with 855 cases at three institutions); Three trial institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: detected 87.32% of breast lesions, against 66.20% without it
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own pre-market reading study. The reference standard was the consensus reading of three imaging experts, not pathology. The CMDE says that long-term safety and effectiveness still need follow-up and asks Deepwise to keep studying how well the algorithm generalizes. The software cannot serve alone as the basis for clinical decisions.

benefit: Fabric GEM helps diagnose an infant in five days by flagging a variant
AI tool: Fabric GEM artificial-intelligence variant interpretation tool with Phevor phenotype-driven re-ranking
deployment context: Rady Children's Institute for Genomic Medicine and Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital; New Brunswick, New Jersey, United States
use-case relevant outcome: clinicians diagnosed an infant within five days
what the sources leave unknown: Neither the authors nor Fabric Genomics separates the parts played by sequencing, GEM, Phevor and clinical review in the speed. The comparison with panels and microarray comes from general turnaround times, and the sources show no test of them in this infant. The authors do not say what became of the pending tests or report her health after the move to palliative care.

benefit: An Emirati health agency adds a chatbot to its website
AI tool: EHS.gov.ae and Ask EHS
deployment context: Emirates Health Services; Northern Emirates, United Arab Emirates
what the sources leave unknown: The agency combines a chatbot with telemedicine, identity services, dashboards and accessibility functions, so no gain can be assigned to AI alone. It gives no measured change in workload, waiting times, access or emissions. Universal coverage and equal access are goals, and a website's availability does not achieve them.

benefit: Vara MG helps German screening radiologists find more breast cancers
AI tool: Vara MG
deployment context: Radiologists at 12 screening units of the German mammography screening program; 12 screening sites, Germany
sample: 463,094 women aged 50 to 69 at 12 sites, July 2021 to February 2023, with 119 radiologists.
use-case relevant outcome: found 6.7 cancers per 1,000 against 5.7 without it
what the sources leave unknown: The study was observational, with no random assignment, and radiologists chose when to use the AI. Vara funded it and took part in its design and writing. It is unclear whether the extra detection lowers interval cancers or improves stage. That will take 2 to 3 years of follow-up. The data came from an early learning phase.

benefit: Dosing by PMD-200 lowered pain scores after abdominal surgery
AI tool: PMD-200 with the Nociception Level (NOL) index
deployment context: Leiden University Medical Center and Alrijne Hospital (SOLAR trial) and Shaare Zedek Medical Center (Abdomi-NOL trial); Leiden and Leiderdorp, Netherlands, and Jerusalem, Israel
use-case relevant outcome: lowered pain scores after abdominal surgery by 30-33%
what the sources leave unknown: Both trials were small, with 50 and 75 patients, and took place in the Netherlands and Israel. They were single-blinded, and pain was the patients' own rating. The gain was measured in the first 90 minutes of recovery. In Abdomi-NOL, no secondary or exploratory outcome, including ward pain scores up to 24 hours, differed significantly between groups.

benefit: AutoEF met its goal for accuracy in measuring how well the heart pumps
AI tool: Caption Interpretation Automated Ejection Fraction Software (AutoEF)
deployment context: Caption Health (retrospective validation on 186 patient studies from three US sites); Minneapolis Heart Institute, Duke University and Northwestern University, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The validation used 186 stored patient studies in a retrospective study that FDA says was conducted to support an earlier clearance, K210747. The reference was expert measurement on 2D echocardiography. The tested model was locked, and later versions will follow the change plan, so they can differ from the one tested.

benefit: Mia flags a 6 mm breast cancer that NHS Grampian radiologists missed
AI tool: Mia
deployment context: NHS Grampian; Aberdeen, United Kingdom
sample: NHS Grampian breast screening, Aberdeen, Scotland, in a program that invites women aged 50 to 71, with 10,889 women screened between 27 February and 5 October 2023.
use-case relevant outcome: 11 additional cancers were found with Mia
what the sources leave unknown: One more cancer was found and treated. The sources do not show that her cancer would otherwise have caused her death or why her radiotherapy lasted five days. The GEMINI authors report that three-year follow-up for interval cancers was not yet available.

benefit: CCAA.91360 cut the time to read cervical cytology slides
developer or vendor: 91360 Medical Technology (Nanjing) Co., Ltd. (玖壹叁陆零医学科技南京有限公司)
AI tool: CCAA.91360 (宫颈细胞学数字病理图像计算机辅助分析软件)
deployment context: 91360 Medical Technology (Nanjing) (registration trial at the First Affiliated Hospital of Nanjing Medical University and the Affiliated Drum Tower Hospital of Nanjing University Medical School); Nanjing, Jiangsu, China
use-case relevant outcome: a mean 64.12 seconds per cervical cytology slide with CCAA.91360, against 333.49 seconds
what the sources leave unknown: 91360 Medical Technology's trial of CCAA.91360 ran at two hospitals with 552 subjects. Each slide was read three ways. Reading time was compared with digital reading alone, and the microscope was the reference for accuracy. The approved use excludes cervical cancer screening and requires pathologists to review the whole image, so the trial does not show time saved in routine work.

benefit: Smartwatch alerts get a 25-year-old treated for atrial fibrillation
developer or vendor: Not stated (the report does not name the device's maker)
AI tool: Smartwatch irregular-rhythm notification (brand and model not stated)
deployment context: Abington, United States (authors' hospital; the report does not name the emergency department)
use-case relevant outcome: atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response at 123 bpm
what the sources leave unknown: The patient also had chest discomfort and palpitations, so the watch’s incremental effect on seeking care is not isolated. The device and algorithm are unnamed, and a general description of watches with AI does not show which model generated this alert. One case is not enough to establish accuracy or the prevention of a future cardiac event.

benefit: GPT-4 flags a cause of a dog's anemia that a second vet then confirms
AI tool: ChatGPT Plus (GPT-4)
deployment context: OpenAI
what the sources leave unknown: The owner reports that GPT-4 listed IMHA and that a second veterinarian confirmed and treated it. No veterinarian has corroborated the account, and no medical record is public. The recovery after treatment does not show whether the dog would otherwise have died or whether the diagnosis depended on AI.

benefit: Opioid Halo cut non-actionable alarms in monitoring for overdose
AI tool: Masimo SafetyNet Opioid System (Opioid Halo software)
deployment context: Masimo (clinical validation on 40,322 data segments from 641 opioid users); Sites not stated in the decision summary (prescription home, hospital and illicit opioid users)
what the sources leave unknown: FDA reviewed Masimo's own analysis of 40,322 recorded data segments from 641 opioid users, not alarms raised during live monitoring. Responsiveness rests on 17 rescues from illicit opioids. FDA credits no rescue to the device, and no outcome for a monitored person is reported.

benefit: Five early cancers are found after qXR flags nodules on unrelated X-rays
AI tool: qXR
deployment context: Participating centers of the CREATE study, not named in the paper; the clinical authors are affiliated with Hacettepe University (Ankara) and with Aarthi Scans and Sri Ramachandra Medical College and Hospital (Chennai)
use-case relevant outcome: confirmed early-stage lung cancer in five adults, and four had surgery
what the sources leave unknown: The authors of the series do not say whether radiologists found the same nodules on their own. So earlier detection by AI, comparative rates of false positives and any survival benefit remain unresolved.

benefit: EA PC-LGI helped endoscopists find more polyps in a Chinese trial
developer or vendor: Wuhan EndoAngel Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (武汉楚精灵医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: EA PC-LGI (肠息肉电子下消化道内窥镜图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Wuhan EndoAngel Medical Technology (prospective trial at Ruijin Hospital, Beijing Cancer Hospital and the Central Hospital of Wuhan); Shanghai, Beijing and Wuhan, China
use-case relevant outcome: detected 84.97% of polyps, against 72.07% in colonoscopies without it
what the sources leave unknown: EndoAngel sponsored the trial and supplied EA PC-LGI. Endoscopists knew when the software was on, and the authors cannot rule out bias. The overall polyp detection rate did not differ between the groups. The primary outcomes were endoscopist sensitivity and specificity, so the trial did not measure cancer outcomes. The trial ran at three large centers in China.

benefit: MY-CJ-01 raised detection of polyps on a first pass in Tencent's trial
developer or vendor: Tencent Healthcare (Shenzhen) Co., Ltd. (腾讯医疗健康（深圳）有限公司)
AI tool: MY-CJ-01 (结肠息肉电子内窥镜图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Tencent Healthcare (Shenzhen) (prospective randomized trial with 296 patients at two centers); Two trial centers that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: The polyp miss rate was 23.39%, against 44.67% in group A
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was Tencent's own, at two centers, with 265 of 296 patients analyzed. CMDE's summary does not say how group A and group B used MY-CJ-01. The endpoint was polyp detection on a first pass, not any outcome of care. The software's marks are for reference only, and the physician must judge whether a polyp is present.

benefit: KidneyIntelX.dkd sorted diabetic patients by risk to their kidneys
AI tool: KidneyIntelX.dkd
deployment context: Renalytix (retrospective validation on biobanked samples from 657 adults); A single biorepository drawing on 10 clinical sites (not named in the decision summary)
what the sources leave unknown: Renalytix, the maker, ran the validation as a retrospective analysis of stored samples from one biorepository. Follow-up was incomplete, so the five-year rates are Kaplan-Meier estimates. Only 55 adults fell in the high level. The submission held no information on patient perspectives. Anthem reports that the evidence comes largely from retrospective and observational studies and shows no meaningful gain in patient-centered outcomes.

benefit: EU guideline group backs AI-supported double reading of mammograms
developer or vendor: Three vendors that asked to remain anonymous in the study behind the estimate, with ScreenPoint Medical (Transpara), Lunit (INSIGHT MMG), Kheiron Medical Technologies (Mia) and DeepHealth in the other studies reviewed
AI tool: AI support for double reading of screening mammograms: three commercial algorithms kept anonymous in the study behind the estimate, with Transpara, Lunit INSIGHT MMG, Mia and a DeepHealth model in the other studies reviewed
deployment context: Screening services in the studies that the ECIBC guideline group reviewed, with Karolinska University Hospital's archived examinations behind the estimate and organized screening programs in the EU as intended users; European Union (guideline), with the study behind the estimate in Stockholm, Sweden
use-case relevant outcome: one more breast cancer for every 1,000 women screened
what the sources leave unknown: The ECIBC group rated the evidence as of very low certainty because the accuracy of the readings is uncertain and no data show effects on breast cancer or mortality. No study used the readings in a screening program or followed women over time. The group calls for prospective studies that measure outcomes such as breast cancer and mortality.

benefit: Lung screening centers may use AI nodule detection under NICE guidance
developer or vendor: Siemens Healthineers, Coreline Soft, Riverain Technologies, contextflow, Infervision, Arterys, Qure.ai, SenseTime, MeVis, Aidence and VUNO
AI tool: AI-derived computer-aided detection software for lung nodules: AI-Rad Companion Chest CT, AVIEW LCS+, ClearRead CT, contextflow SEARCH Lung CT, InferRead CT Lung, Lung AI, qCT-Lung, SenseCare-Lung Pro, Veolity, Veye Lung Nodules and VUNO Med-LungCT AI
deployment context: Screening centers in the studies reviewed by NICE and NHS targeted lung cancer screening centers in England during evidence generation; England, United Kingdom (guidance), with studies in several countries
use-case relevant outcome: In all nine studies of reading time, review was faster with the software
what the sources leave unknown: NICE found five studies, on four products, with per-person screening results, and none compared products. Its cost model was exploratory and indicative only. The reading-time studies were partly in laboratory-like conditions. Five of the 13 products had no published evidence. A 2026 IQWiG report on AI reading of chest images found no studies of patient-relevant outcomes.

benefit: EASYASPECT brought doctors' scores of stroke CT closer to experts'
developer or vendor: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology Co., Ltd. (语坤（北京）网络科技有限公司)
AI tool: EASYASPECT (缺血性卒中CT图像辅助评估软件)
deployment context: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology (retrospective reader trial at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Nanchang University and Hwa Mei Hospital of the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences in Ningbo); Ningbo, Zhejiang and Nanchang, Jiangxi, China
use-case relevant outcome: a kappa of 0.80 with EASYASPECT, against 0.55 without it
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was retrospective, with 224 past scans, two hospitals and 8 doctors. Its main outcome was agreement with an expert panel, not patient outcomes. CMDE says that the software cannot serve alone as a basis for treatment decisions and must not be used in emergency care.

benefit: Viz HCM picked out a hard-to-diagnose heart disease from ECGs
AI tool: Viz HCM
deployment context: Viz.ai (retrospective study on ECGs from three Massachusetts hospitals); Boston area and Salem, Massachusetts, United States
sample: 3,196 ECGs (291 with and 2,905 without hypertrophic cardiomyopathy) from three Massachusetts hospitals, 2017 to 2022.
use-case relevant outcome: a sensitivity of 68.4% and a specificity of 99.1%
what the sources leave unknown: The study used historical patient data from three Massachusetts hospitals and involved no patients. A single cardiologist labeled each ECG, and a second cardiologist rechecked only 60. Usability testing involved cardiologists, not non-specialist clinicians. The submission did not include patient perspectives.

benefit: A surgical robot helps a surgeon remove a brain clot from an awake man
AI tool: Modus V Synaptive robotic digital microscope with Neuro-Navigation AI (image fusion, fiber-tract display, surgical simulation, trajectory warnings)
deployment context: Tam Anh General Hospital, Ho Chi Minh City; Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
use-case relevant outcome: About 40 ml of clot came out in just over 30 minutes
what the sources leave unknown: Several teams took part in the operation, so its outcome cannot be credited to the software alone. The hospital gives no comparison of this patient's outcome with conventional surgery, and no long-term neurological follow-up is reported. In its account, the hospital calls the gap between a 14:00 arrival and a 17:00 start two hours.

benefit: DrBrain-AD flagged hippocampal changes on brain MRI in China's review
developer or vendor: Shenzhen Yiwei Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (深圳市铱硙医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: DrBrain-AD (磁共振图像辅助评估软件)
deployment context: Shenzhen Yiwei Medical Technology (registration trial with 514 patients at three hospitals); Xuanwu Hospital of Capital Medical University, the Second Xiangya Hospital of Central South University and the First Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University, China
use-case relevant outcome: a sensitivity of 0.9328 and a specificity of 0.9042
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was single-arm and multicenter, run by the applicant, with 514 patients at three hospitals. There was no unaided reading arm, so the report gives no figures for doctors reading without the software. The targets came from pre-clinical data and guideline consensus.

benefit: AI100 with Shonit matched manual microscopy on 882 blood smears
AI tool: AI100 with Shonit
deployment context: SigTuple (method comparison against manual microscopy at four sites)
use-case relevant outcome: 92.7% sensitivity and 95.4% specificity for abnormal white cells
what the sources leave unknown: The study measured agreement with manual microscopy at four sites, not accuracy against a clinical diagnosis or any effect on care. It did not measure time saved. Agreement was weakest for monocytes, with a correlation of 0.789. Results depend on a skilled operator, who identifies and classifies each cell.

benefit: NICE finds AI outlining quicker for radiotherapy planning
developer or vendor: Siemens Healthineers, TheraPanacea, Mirada Medical, Carina Medical, Limbus AI, MIM Software, Philips, MVision AI and RaySearch
AI tool: AI autocontouring software: AI-Rad Companion Organs RT, ART-Plan, DLCExpert, INTContour, Limbus Contour, MIM Contour ProtégéAI, MRCAT Prostate plus Auto-contouring, MVision Segmentation Service and RayStation
deployment context: Radiotherapy centers in the studies reviewed by NICE; NHS radiotherapy services in England; Multiple countries (studies); England, United Kingdom (guidance)
sample: 79 studies, with data extracted from 15 priority studies, 8 prospective.
use-case relevant outcome: Reported time savings ranged from 3 to 80 minutes
what the sources leave unknown: Of the 79 studies NICE found, 52 were conference abstracts. Some reported time savings left out review and editing time. Only four technologies had evidence on radiation dose, and all lacked long-term patient outcomes such as radiation toxicity. No evidence covered children or people with atypical anatomy. In a 2026 evaluation in eight NHS departments, faster contouring did not shorten the whole planning pathway.

benefit: EC01-01 helped endoscopists find more colon polyps in a trial
developer or vendor: Xiamen Yingnuo Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (厦门影诺医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: EC01-01 (肠息肉电子下消化道图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Xiamen Yingnuo Medical Technology (prospective parallel-controlled trial with 1,020 subjects at four sites); Four trial sites in China that the report does not name
use-case relevant outcome: detected 94.7% of polyps, against 84.5% without it
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own, a prospective parallel-controlled study at four Chinese sites, and the report does not say whether patients were randomized. The reference came from two experts reading the recorded videos, with a third settling disagreements. CMDE says the output is for reference only and no clinical decision may rest on it alone.

benefit: AI-SONIC-TH flagged suspicious thyroid nodules in China's review
developer or vendor: Zhejiang Deshang Yunxing Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (浙江德尚韵兴医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: AI-SONIC-TH (甲状腺结节超声影像辅助诊断软件)
deployment context: Zhejiang Deshang Yunxing Medical Technology (prospective registration trial with 1,043 patients at three sites); Three trial sites that the report does not name, for a registration in China
what the sources leave unknown: The evidence is the maker's own trial of 1,043 patients at three sites, whose primary endpoint was the software's accuracy reading alone, against a reference that the report does not state. Doctors reading alone were not reported, so the software's effect on doctors is unmeasured. A sonographer must outline each nodule by hand, and no patient outcome is reported.

benefit: AneurDoc flagged aneurysms on CT angiograms in China's review
developer or vendor: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology Co., Ltd. (语坤（北京）网络科技有限公司)
AI tool: AneurDoc (颅内动脉瘤CT血管造影图像辅助分诊软件)
deployment context: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology (prospective multicenter registration trial with 486 cases); General Hospital of the PLA Northern Theater Command and Huangshi Central Hospital, China
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own, a prospective single-arm study of 486 patients at two hospitals, judged against an expert panel's reading rather than against patient outcomes. CMDE restricts AneurDoc to trained doctors and says it cannot be the sole basis of a clinical decision.

benefit: Medical students trained with a ChatZOC digital patient score higher
developer or vendor: Zhongshan Ophthalmic Center, Sun Yat-sen University
AI tool: ChatZOC ophthalmology model
deployment context: Multiple regions in China (pilots)
sample: Study 1: 84 fourth-year clinical medicine students at the Zhongshan School of Medicine, Sun Yat-sen University. The trial had a single center and was registered as NCT06229379. Study 2: ChatZOC and 10 other language models, including GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 Turbo, with no patients involved.
what the sources leave unknown: The center claims lower misdiagnosis and better early diagnosis without an outcome denominator, a comparator or follow-up. The randomized trial of 84 medical students measured history-taking scores and reported no patient outcome. No patient outcome from the clinical pilots had appeared by October 2026.

benefit: LiverMRDoc reached judgments on liver MRI faster in China's review
developer or vendor: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology Co., Ltd. (语坤（北京）网络科技有限公司)
AI tool: LiverMRDoc (肝脏局灶性病变MR图像辅助分诊软件)
deployment context: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology (retrospective registration trial with 490 cases at two hospitals); Beijing Friendship Hospital of Capital Medical University in Beijing and Ningbo Hwa Mei Hospital of the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences in Ningbo, China
use-case relevant outcome: a median of 7.47 minutes with LiverMRDoc, against 9.45 minutes for an expert panel
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was retrospective and single-group, judging the software against performance targets and an expert panel's results. It ran at two hospitals. Judgment time was a secondary measure, compared with the same panel that set the reference standard. The applicant supplied the trial.

benefit: A geneticist confirms Alström syndrome after ChatGPT lists a gene
AI tool: ChatGPT
deployment context: Medical University of Vienna, Division of Nephrology and Dialysis; Vienna, Austria
use-case relevant outcome: confirmed Alström syndrome in two business days
what the sources leave unknown: The two business days are the time from the suggestion to genetic confirmation. One case cannot show how quickly clinicians would otherwise have found the condition, or whether the diagnosis changed the patient's later health.

benefit: NaviCam ProScan helped doctors find more lesions in less time
AI tool: NaviCam ProScan
deployment context: Seven European centers in the prospective ARTIC study (22 capsule endoscopy readers); Seven centers in Italy, France, Germany, Hungary, Spain, Sweden and the United Kingdom
what the sources leave unknown: The study enrolled 133 patients at seven European centers and did not collect race or ethnicity. Performance of the device without clinician input was not evaluated, so standalone performance was not established, and the number of false positive predictions from the software alone is unknown. FDA requires postmarket testing to show how the device performs in use.

benefit: Older adults describe satisfaction with AI companions at senior centers
AI tool: ESTsoft AI Senior Care Content and conversational companion
deployment context: Gimhae City smart senior centers; Gimhae, South Korea; additional Japanese pilots
sample: 40 older adults across 10 smart senior centers in Gimhae, South Korea, using the service for six weeks or more.
what the sources leave unknown: ESTsoft reports that 40 interviewed users in 10 Gimhae centers described physical, psychological and social satisfaction, and it gives no measured health outcome. Use in 36 centers and a demonstration with 500 participants show reported activity. No outcome measure, comparison group or follow-up for cognitive, physical or emotional improvement has been reported.

benefit: Pilots test software that analyzes the gait of horses
AI tool: AIforPet horse-identification and gait-analysis platform
deployment context: not in the sources
what the sources leave unknown: Pilot feasibility and acceptance do not show accurate identification or gait classification across breeds, ages and activities. The maker gives no sample, validation design, error rates, veterinary decisions or measured change in welfare.

benefit: DERM triages suspected skin cancer safely at four NHS sites
AI tool: DERM (Deep Ensemble for the Recognition of Malignancy)
deployment context: Chelsea and Westminster, University Hospitals Bristol and Weston, Ashford and St Peter's and University Hospitals Birmingham NHS foundation trusts, with Birmingham primary care networks; London, Bristol, Surrey and Birmingham, England, United Kingdom
what the sources leave unknown: Without granular baseline data, the evaluators could not separate DERM's effect from that of existing pathways. The teledermatology comparison data were skewed toward best-in-class sites, which likely inflated the return on investment. Data on missed cancers and on quality of life were limited. Few lesions were seen at the Birmingham community hub. NICE notes that DERM was evaluated mainly in people with white skin.

benefit: Koios DS Breast helped readers classify breast lumps on ultrasound
AI tool: Koios DS Breast
deployment context: Readers in the four retrospective studies that AQuAS reviewed, three in the United States and one in Spain; Spain (assessment), with studies in the United States and Spain
what the sources leave unknown: AQuAS names retrospective designs, which do not capture all aspects of a real clinical setting, as the main limitation. It found a high risk of selection bias that could overstate sensitivity. Specificity was assessed in only one study, with no statistical test. It found insufficient evidence on early detection and says that prospective studies in a real clinical setting are needed.

benefit: AI echocardiography assistants match experts' ejection fractions
developer or vendor: Caption Health (Caption Guidance), GE HealthCare (Real-Time EF), DIA Imaging Analysis (LVivo Seamless) and EchoNous (AI TRIO)
AI tool: AI echocardiography assistants: Caption Guidance, Real-Time EF, LVivo Seamless and AI TRIO
deployment context: Hospitals in the five validation studies that AETSA reviewed, in the United States, Germany, Tunisia and Portugal; United States, Germany, Tunisia and Portugal (studies), assessed for Spain
use-case relevant outcome: intraclass correlation was 0.84 for Caption Guidance
what the sources leave unknown: AETSA found risks of bias because index or reference results were not masked and patients were not selected consecutively. The studies enrolled few patients. No large longitudinal studies establish the diagnostic validity of the ejection fractions. AETSA found no data on use in Europe.

benefit: Ethos daily replanning improves tumor coverage in Malaysia's review
developer or vendor: Varian Medical Systems (a Siemens Healthineers company)
AI tool: Ethos therapy (Varian Ethos online adaptive radiotherapy)
deployment context: Several radiotherapy centers in the 10 studies that MaHTAS reviewed, among them University Hospital Essen, UT Southwestern Medical Center, Rigshospitalet and Medisch Spectrum Twente; Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, the United States, Australia and China (studies that MaHTAS reviewed)
use-case relevant outcome: 99.4% with the adapted plans and 86.7% with the scheduled plans
what the sources leave unknown: The evidence is 10 observational studies of 244 patients. Outcomes were short-term dosimetric measures. No study reported survival, tumor control or long-term toxicity. Follow-up was short. Safety evidence was limited. MaHTAS found no evidence on cost or cost-effectiveness.

benefit: BrainSee predicted which patients with memory loss would get dementia
AI tool: BrainSee
deployment context: Darmiyan (retrospective validation on 198 patients from 27 North American sites); 27 North American sites
what the sources leave unknown: The validation was retrospective, on archived data from 198 patients, after 209 eligible patients without five years of follow-up were left out. The lower confidence bound for sensitivity fell below the 70% goal. Nearly 90% of patients were white, which FDA says leaves performance in other groups uncertain. No clinician acted on a score, so no effect on care is shown.

benefit: DermaSensor raised primary care sensitivity for skin cancer
AI tool: DermaSensor
deployment context: Primary care sites in the DERM-SUCCESS study; Twenty-two sites in the United States and Australia
sample: Study 1: 108 physicians in internal medicine or family practice, who read 25 malignant and 25 benign lesions. Study 2: 1,005 patients, 1,579 lesions, 22 sites in the US and Australia.
what the sources leave unknown: The 91.4% aided sensitivity comes from a reader study in which 108 physicians viewed 50 lesion images, not from live use. Physicians in the pivotal study were blinded to the device output. FDA says that real-world use may differ from the premarket studies. Darker skin types were poorly represented, and the maker funded all key studies.

benefit: Fibresolve flagged more lung fibrosis than experts in FDA's review
AI tool: Fibresolve
deployment context: Imvaria (retrospective study on 300 CT cases from the Lung Tissue Research Consortium); Lung Tissue Research Consortium sites (not named in the decision summary)
what the sources leave unknown: The test set was archived scans from 2005 to 2018, so results may not hold for modern equipment, and the reference diagnoses may not reflect current practice. The comparator was a five-member expert panel reading charts. FDA found only a small probable benefit and requires a postmarket study on modern images for the on-label slice thicknesses.

benefit: Man regains movement in a paralyzed replanted arm
developer or vendor: Center for Bionics and Pain Research / University of Gothenburg (academic clinical team); device by Integrum AB
AI tool: Myoelectric motor execution with sensory training: Neuromotus 8-channel EMG and LDA classifier driving virtual limbs and serious games
deployment context: Center for Bionics and Pain Research and Sahlgrenska University Hospital (C.A.R.E.), Mölndal; treatment site not named in the paper; Mölndal, Sweden
sample: One 72-year-old man with a replanted right arm and no functional recovery after conventional rehabilitation, Sweden.
use-case relevant outcome: active thumb extension (4 degrees) and active wrist flexion (6 degrees)
what the sources leave unknown: The intervention combined decoded motor execution, repeated practice and sensory training, and one case without controls cannot separate their parts. The authors give no treatment dates and report no follow-up after the final session.

benefit: CAD4TB falls just short of WHO's target for TB screening in Africa
AI tool: CAD4TB, with qXR in one study (computer-aided detection software for TB)
deployment context: Active case-finding programs and national TB prevalence surveys in Kenya, South Africa and Zambia (five studies); Kenya, South Africa and Zambia
what the sources leave unknown: All five studies carried a high risk of bias, and three set their thresholds after the analysis. All five excluded people inappropriately, for example by testing sputum only from those with symptoms or abnormal x-rays. The review could not pool results for people with HIV. It covered only people aged 15 and older and only English-language studies.

benefit: Faster stroke treatment followed e-Stroke, RapidAI and Viz
AI tool: e-Stroke, RapidAI and Viz (AI-derived software for CT brain scans in suspected stroke)
deployment context: NHS stroke centers in England, with AI decision support live at 99 of 107 stroke units; England, United Kingdom
what the sources leave unknown: The NICE assessors found only retrospective before-and-after studies at high risk of bias. Before and after populations may have differed, and the software may not have been the only change to stroke care. The studies included only people with a positive scan, so delays after a false negative are unknown. No eligible study measured accuracy with clinician review, and results on clinical outcomes conflicted.

benefit: A 76-year-old spots a change on his Apple Watch ECG, leading to a bypass
AI tool: Apple Watch ECG app (single lead-I recording; its rhythm classifier is not mentioned in the report)
deployment context: Amsterdam, the Netherlands
what the sources leave unknown: The sources do not show that AI detected ischemia. The wearer noticed the change in the T-wave, and clinicians interpreted the tests that followed. The watch’s separate atrial-fibrillation feature does not supply that missing causal link. This is a documented pathway of care assisted by a device, and whether it counts as a benefit of AI is unresolved.

benefit: Genius Cervical AI helped cytology teams catch more precancers
AI tool: Genius Digital Diagnostics System with the Genius Cervical AI algorithm
deployment context: Four US cytology laboratories in Hologic's multi-center clinical study; Four cytology laboratories, United States
what the sources leave unknown: In the Genius Cervical AI study, residual slides were read after sign-out, so no patient's care depended on the result. The digital review always came last, after microscope reading, and the slides included many abnormal categories. The gain at the ASCUS threshold was not significant, and cancer sensitivity did not differ. Four experienced laboratories took part.

benefit: A nurse returns to full-time work after software detects her brain bleed
AI tool: Viz.ai stroke detection and care coordination (attribution inferred)
deployment context: Baptist Health, Marcus Neuroscience Institute; Boca Raton, Florida, United States
what the sources leave unknown: Baptist Health has not confirmed which product, module or release flagged this patient's scan. No source isolates the software's effect on survival.

benefit: NICE lets NHS talking therapies use the Limbic Access chatbot
AI tool: Limbic Access (AI self-referral chatbot)
deployment context: NHS Talking Therapies for anxiety and depression services in England; England, United Kingdom
sample: 129,400 patients in NHS Talking Therapies services in England.
use-case relevant outcome: referrals rise by 15%, against 6% in control services
what the sources leave unknown: The 15% rise comes from an observational study. NICE says that most evidence came from the companies or from authors affiliated with them. It found a lack of evidence on people who could not access the service. It says that it is unclear whether the evidence applies to all NHS providers. It says that evidence on time saved is limited.

benefit: Samsung's Sleep Apnea Feature caught most moderate to severe cases
AI tool: Sleep Apnea Feature (Samsung Galaxy Watch and Phone)
deployment context: Samsung (multi-center clinical validation against polysomnography run by an accredited sleep lab); Sites not named in the decision summary
what the sources leave unknown: The study enrolled an enriched population, and 47 of 620 enrolled subjects did not finish. The feature gave no usable result on 16.7% of nights. The specificity target was met only after a post-hoc analysis. Subgroups were not powered for conclusive comparisons. FDA says that 10 people were directed to care but reports no follow-up.

benefit: Dr.Wise-AADS helped doctors find more brain aneurysms on CT
developer or vendor: Hangzhou Deepwise (杭州深睿博联科技有限公司)
AI tool: Dr.Wise-AADS (颅内动脉瘤CT造影图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Hangzhou Deepwise (retrospective crossover reader trial on 965 cases at four institutions); Four trial institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: lesion-level sensitivity for brain aneurysms on CT angiograms 10.85% higher
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the applicant's own retrospective crossover study. Doctors read stored scans, and imaging experts' readings were the reference. It measured sensitivity and specificity, not patient outcomes. The software assists detection of only some aneurysms, those of 3 mm or more.

benefit: EndoBRAIN-EYE wins a Japanese insurance add-on for better colonoscopy
developer or vendor: Cybernet Systems Co., Ltd. (サイバネットシステム株式会社), with Showa University Northern Yokohama Hospital and Nagoya University
AI tool: EndoBRAIN-EYE (内視鏡画像診断支援プログラム)
deployment context: Japanese hospitals and clinics where colonoscopy specialists use it during polyp removal (not named); Japan
what the sources leave unknown: The 21.6% to 31.2% figure for EndoBRAIN-EYE comes from a trade journal's report of Cybernet's press conference, where it is the result of a clinical performance test. The ministry's Q&A names the product and approval number and cites no figures. The measure is specialists' detection rate, not patient outcomes. The add-on requires a physician with at least five years of experience.

benefit: Wales supports CADe colonoscopy after it found more adenomas in trials
developer or vendor: Medtronic (GI Genius), Olympus (ENDO-AID), Fujifilm (CAD EYE), Wision AI (EndoScreener), Wuhan EndoAngel Medical Technology Company (EndoAngel) and other makers
AI tool: Computer-aided detection (CADe) colonoscopy systems in the trials that HTW pooled, including GI Genius, ENDO-AID, CAD EYE, EndoScreener and EndoAngel
deployment context: Endoscopy services in the pooled randomized trials; Multiple countries (trials), with guidance for Wales, United Kingdom
use-case relevant outcome: 23% higher with CADe than with standard colonoscopy
what the sources leave unknown: The main source of bias was that endoscopists and outcome assessors were not blinded. HTW reports high heterogeneity and wide confidence intervals. It found no evidence that CADe raised detection of advanced adenomas or of carcinoma, which was rare. No study reported subsequent surgery, time to diagnosis or quality of life. HTW asked for data on real-world use.

benefit: Sepsis ImmunoScore sorted patients by sepsis risk in FDA's review
AI tool: Sepsis ImmunoScore
deployment context: Prenosis (retrospective validation on data from three US hospitals); Boston, Massachusetts; Chicago, Illinois; Royal Oak, Michigan, United States
sample: 746 patients with suspected sepsis at three US hospitals.
use-case relevant outcome: an area under the ROC curve of 0.81
what the sources leave unknown: The study was retrospective, using data collected prospectively at three hospitals, so the score guided no care. Physicians at the patients' own hospitals judged who had sepsis, though FDA recommends independent adjudicators at separate institutions. Only 33 patients fell in the very high group, and its 95% interval for sepsis ran from 51.29% to 84.41%.

benefit: Rho detects low bone density on routine x-rays but misses many cases
AI tool: Rho
deployment context: 16 Bit (retrospective study on x-rays from True North Imaging, OneMedNet and the Osteoarthritis Initiative); Six True North Imaging centers in Ontario, Canada, and US sites of OneMedNet and the Osteoarthritis Initiative
what the sources leave unknown: The accuracy comes from archived x-rays paired with DXA scans, and no patient was referred because of the software. The device missed the sponsor's original co-primary goals for sensitivity and specificity and met its goals for specificity and AUC. FDA notes uncertainty about the lower sensitivity in the US datasets and in some subgroups.

benefit: A stage I cancer is removed in Chiayi after AI colonoscopy flags a polyp
AI tool: Fujifilm AI endoscopy system on a Fujifilm 7000-series gastrointestinal endoscope (product name not given in the sources)
deployment context: St. Martin De Porres Hospital (天主教聖馬爾定醫院), Chiayi; Chiayi, Taiwan
sample: 361 people aged 50 to 74 with a positive fecal immunochemical test, one hospital in Palencia, Spain, October 2023 to February 2025.
use-case relevant outcome: a 1 to 1.5 cm adenoma that biopsy confirmed as stage I colorectal cancer
what the sources leave unknown: A positive stool test had already prompted the examination, and pathology established the cancer. The hospital's account does not show that the endoscopist would otherwise have missed the lesion or that the AI spared the man more invasive treatment. The authors of the 2026 trial in Palencia found that CAD EYE did not raise adenoma detection in patients referred after a positive stool test. No recurrence or survival data are reported.

benefit: FDA qualified the AFib History Feature for trials of ablation devices
AI tool: Apple Atrial Fibrillation History Feature
deployment context: Apple (prospective AFib History clinical study of 280 subjects)
use-case relevant outcome: differed from an ECG patch by 0.67% on average
what the sources leave unknown: The evidence comes from Apple's own study for the feature's earlier clearance, not from ablation trials. Only 36 subjects had a prior ablation, in a post-hoc analysis, and their upper limit of agreement exceeded the 15% criterion. FDA notes that reduced heart rate variability after ablation could harm accuracy.

benefit: AI biopsy review catches more prostate cancers in HTW's pooled studies
developer or vendor: Ibex Medical Analytics (Galen Prostate), Paige AI (Paige Prostate) and Deep Bio (DeepDx Prostate)
AI tool: AI-assisted review of prostate biopsies: Galen Prostate, Paige Prostate and DeepDx Prostate
deployment context: Pathology services in the studies that HTW reviewed, with Galen Prostate introduced across NHS Wales through a Welsh Government innovation fund pilot; Multiple countries (studies), with guidance for Wales, United Kingdom
what the sources leave unknown: HTW's pooled sensitivity figure combines four studies of two different AI tools with high heterogeneity. Peer-reviewed evidence is limited, and none of the studies measured patient outcomes. NICE's briefing, which HTW cites, found the studies mainly retrospective and not based in the UK.

benefit: ColoSense stool RNA test found 25 of 27 colorectal cancers
AI tool: ColoSense
deployment context: Geneoscopy (CRC-PREVENT study with participants from 48 US states); United States (48 contiguous states)
what the sources leave unknown: Only 27 cancers were in the study, so FDA warns that as many as 24.3% of patients with colorectal cancer may be missed. The model was built with five-fold cross-validation on 939 samples and a hold-out set of 388. Because of this uncertainty, FDA requires post-approval studies to confirm ColoSense's sensitivity. Every participant also had a colonoscopy, so no screening decision rested on the test.

benefit: Notal Vision Home OCT lets patients scan their own retinas at home
AI tool: Notal Vision Home Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT) System with the Notal OCT Analyzer (NOA)
deployment context: Notal Vision (001 Study at seven US sites, with patients imaging themselves at home, and 006 Study at six US sites); Patients' homes and seven US clinical sites (001 Study) and six US sites (006 Study)
what the sources leave unknown: The 001 Study followed patients for about five weeks and was not designed to show that the device works as an early detection tool. FDA states that improved visual outcomes have not been demonstrated. The negative agreement did not significantly exceed its 0.8 target. Almost all participants (96.7%) were White.

benefit: DentalMonitoring reads phone photos of braces for orthodontists
AI tool: DentalMonitoring
deployment context: Dental Monitoring (retrospective and prospective studies with US orthodontists); United States (retrospective review with 15 US orthodontists and prospective studies at US sites)
what the sources leave unknown: The accuracy figures come from retrospective scans judged by panels of three orthodontists, not from treatment results. The bite study used 3D models from intraoral scanners as its reference. Sensitivity was 79.9% for gum recession and 81.0% for black triangles, with 95% intervals from 70.3% to 86.9% and from 73.9% to 86.5%.

benefit: Ant's AI health assistant reaches millions of users in China
AI tool: Ant medical large model and health-assistant agents
deployment context: Zhejiang Provincial Health Commission; Hangzhou Municipal Medical Insurance Bureau; Renji Hospital; China: Zhejiang, Hangzhou, and Shanghai
what the sources leave unknown: The reported 13 million users and 78 million service instances are measures of reach and usage. They are no evidence of better health. The claim of 50% faster annotation has no baseline and no independent evaluation. Accuracy and satisfaction are different measures, and neither stands in for patient outcomes or fair access.

benefit: Kaia's exercise app eased back pain in an independent assessment
AI tool: Kaia app for app-based exercise therapy, rated with DarioHealth's program in the same category
deployment context: Kaia Health, through its app, in two studies of people with back pain in Germany; Germany (studies), with an assessment for US purchasers
what the sources leave unknown: Both Kaia studies lasted 12 weeks, covered back pain in Germany, and carried a high risk of bias. All the included studies used earlier versions of the Kaia app. U.S. pricing is not public, so PHTI did not estimate the budget impact of this category.

benefit: MCS flagged 11 eye diseases on fundus photos in China's review
developer or vendor: Beijing Zhiyuan Huitu Technology Co., Ltd. (北京致远慧图科技有限公司)
AI tool: MCS / MCSLocal (眼底病变眼底图像辅助诊断软件)
deployment context: Beijing Zhiyuan Huitu Technology (registration trial with 2,778 fundus photographs at four institutions); Four trial institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: 91.18% sensitivity and 91.56% specificity for diabetic retinopathy
what the sources leave unknown: The maker's trial was single-arm and compared the software with central reading against preset targets, not with doctors in practice. It excluded poor-quality and special images. CMDE notes that accuracy may fall when a patient has two or more eye diseases and may be slightly lower with some camera models. The trial measured accuracy, not patient outcomes.

benefit: Abridge scribe pilot trimmed EHR time for UChicago clinicians
AI tool: Abridge AI scribe
deployment context: University of Chicago Medicine; University of Chicago Medicine ambulatory clinics, Chicago, Illinois, United States
sample: 125 scribe users and 478 nonusers, University of Chicago ambulatory clinics.
use-case relevant outcome: 15.9% less time in notes and 8.5% less time in the EHR
what the sources leave unknown: The study was retrospective and observational, and the clinicians volunteered. The authors say residual selection bias may remain, such as an early-adopter trait. Epic's EHR-time measures cannot tell active use from time when the EHR is merely open. Patient complexity and use of Dragon dictation were not measured. The pilot lasted three months at one academic health system and covered English-language visits only.

benefit: Smartwatch readings lead to a family's long QT diagnosis
AI tool: Withings ScanWatch ECG with QT monitoring function
deployment context: Mannheim, Germany
use-case relevant outcome: displayed values such as QT 506 ms and QTc 457 ms
what the sources leave unknown: The case report supports the diagnosis, family screening and a measured shortening of the QTc after treatment. Prevention of a future arrhythmic death remains a potential benefit with no observed outcome. Withings has not published what part a learned model plays in the watch's calculation of the QT interval. The authors of a study in 2022 wrote that the watch's algorithm for the QTc needed improvement for clinical use.

benefit: Emory diagnoses VT after a smartwatch ECG records a 165 bpm tachycardia
developer or vendor: Not stated (the report does not name the device's maker)
AI tool: Smartwatch ECG function with high-heart-rate warning (brand and model not stated)
deployment context: Atlanta, United States (authors' institution; the admitting hospital is not named)
use-case relevant outcome: recorded a 165 bpm wide-complex tachycardia during palpitations
what the sources leave unknown: The authors do not name the watch's brand or model, and they give no dates for the events. The watch recorded an ECG and gave a generic warning about the heart rate. Clinicians identified the ventricular tachycardia. No source quantifies how much earlier treatment occurred.

benefit: Oura ring trends guide a Holter that shows 2,078 PVCs in 24 h
developer or vendor: Maker of the ŌURA ring (company not named in the paper)
AI tool: ŌURA ring (heart-rate and heart-rate-variability summaries) used within GluCare.Health's hybrid care model
deployment context: GluCare.Health, Dubai; Dubai, United Arab Emirates
use-case relevant outcome: 24-hour Holter recorded 2,078 ventricular events (1.75% of beats, no couplets or runs)
what the sources leave unknown: The ring did not detect PVCs or issue an alert. Its readings added context to an assessment that clinicians led, partly in retrospect, and the authors are inconsistent about when that review happened. Neither the presence of a learned model nor an outcome caused by it is established.

benefit: LiverMRDoc Pro helped doctors find more liver lesions on MRI
developer or vendor: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology Co., Ltd. (语坤（北京）网络科技有限公司)
AI tool: LiverMRDoc Pro (肝脏局灶性病变MR图像辅助评估软件)
deployment context: Yukun (Beijing) Network Technology (retrospective reader trial on 392 cases at five hospitals); Beijing Friendship Hospital of Capital Medical University, Ningbo Hwa Mei Hospital of the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Affiliated Hospital of Hebei University, First Affiliated Hospital of Xi'an Jiaotong University and Huazhong University of Science and Technology Union Shenzhen Hospital, China
use-case relevant outcome: lesion-level sensitivity for focal liver lesions 0.0969 higher
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was retrospective, with readers assessing stored images from 392 enrolled subjects at five hospitals. The applicant ran it, and expert consensus served as the reference standard. The report gives detection rates and reading times, with no patient outcomes.

benefit: Shield blood test found most colorectal cancers but few precancers
AI tool: Shield
deployment context: Guardant Health (ECLIPSE study at 265 US sites); 265 sites, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The study found only 65 colorectal cancers, 22 at stage I, so the stage I estimate is imprecise. It was cross-sectional, and the benefits and risks of repeated testing over time have not been studied. FDA says that sensitivity compared with other screening methods has not been established. A three-year post-approval study was required.

benefit: IR-CT-AO flagged aortic dissections in a prospective trial in China
developer or vendor: Infervision Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (推想医疗科技股份有限公司)
AI tool: IR-CT-AO (主动脉夹层CT造影图像辅助评估软件), models IR-CT-AO (A) and IR-CT-AO (B)
deployment context: Infervision Medical Technology (prospective trial with 485 subjects); Trial centers in China that the report does not name
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was single-arm against targets of 80%, with no comparison group. Three physicians reading the images set the reference, not surgery or other tests. The trial excluded poor-quality images and patients treated earlier for the aorta. CMDE says that the software cannot serve alone as evidence for clinical decisions.

benefit: AIneurysm helped doctors find more brain aneurysms on MR scans
developer or vendor: Fuying (Shanghai) Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (复影（上海）医疗科技有限公司). The Paper reports that a Fudan University team led by Professor Geng Daoying developed the software.
AI tool: AIneurysm (颅内动脉瘤磁共振图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Fuying (Shanghai) Medical Technology (retrospective reader trial on 484 analyzed cases from three centers); Three trial centers that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: lesion-level sensitivity for brain aneurysms on MR angiograms by 0.0698
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was retrospective, so the doctors read stored MR angiograms and no patient's care depended on AIneurysm. Fuying, the applicant, ran it. The reference standard was an expert panel's markings rather than patient outcomes. CMDE states that the software is for trained doctors and cannot serve alone as a basis for clinical decisions.

benefit: SELENA+ results on the spot bring more Tanzanians to eye care
AI tool: SELENA+
deployment context: London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine and Kilimanjaro Christian Medical Centre, with diabetes clinics in 24 hospitals; Kilimanjaro and Arusha regions, Tanzania
sample: 2,378 adults with diabetes at 24 hospitals in Kilimanjaro and Arusha, 8 March 2023 to 31 August 2024, of whom 904 had referable disease.
use-case relevant outcome: raised clinic attendance for referable retinopathy from 18.2% to 35.9%
what the sources leave unknown: The trial compared two whole pathways, so the instant SELENA+ result cannot be separated from face-to-face counseling. Participants knew their group. The primary outcome was clinic attendance within eight weeks. The trial was not powered to show more treatment or better vision.

benefit: AI microscope saves time on cancer tests at St. Olavs hospital
developer or vendor: Not named (the supplier of the microscope)
AI tool: AI cell classifier built into a CE-IVD certified fluorescence microscope for FISH analysis (product not named)
deployment context: St. Olavs hospital HF, Trondheim; Trondheim, Norway
what the sources leave unknown: The auditor says that the systems, other than the tax agency's model, have not been systematically evaluated, and it gives no figures for St. Olavs. The comparison is with earlier manual work, and the AI is only one part of the new microscope. As the first buyer in Norway, the hospital had no references for validating the AI.

benefit: uAI-PulmonaryEmbolism flagged pulmonary embolism in China's review
developer or vendor: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence Co., Ltd. (上海联影智能医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: uAI-PulmonaryEmbolism (肺栓塞CT血管造影图像辅助分诊软件)
deployment context: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence (retrospective trial with 496 cases at three institutions); Three trial institutions in China that the report does not name
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own retrospective study on stored images. It tested the software against target values, not against doctors reading without it. An expert panel's reading was the reference. The report names processing time as a secondary endpoint but gives no result. The software cannot serve alone as the basis for clinical decisions.

benefit: Yunnan Baiyao reports faster herb sorting with its Leigong model
developer or vendor: Huawei Technologies Co., Ltd. and Yunnan Baiyao Group Co., Ltd.
AI tool: Leigong large model for traditional Chinese medicine
deployment context: Yunnan Baiyao Group Co., Ltd.; Yunnan, China
what the sources leave unknown: The companies combine several applications and give no measurement method for the 30–50-fold sorting gain, the CNY 50 million cut in returns or the change in satisfaction. Their claim of a 300% gain in accuracy also needs a baseline and a metric. Gross savings exclude implementation costs, and neither satisfaction nor manufacturing efficiency shows clinical effectiveness.

benefit: uAI-CTA-HeadNeckVessels helped doctors find more brain aneurysms
developer or vendor: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence Co., Ltd. (上海联影智能医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: uAI-CTA-HeadNeckVessels (颅内动脉瘤CT造影图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence (retrospective reader trial on 484 cases at three institutions); Three trial institutions that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: detected 90.00% of intracranial aneurysms on CT angiograms, against 81.97% without it
what the sources leave unknown: The applicant ran the trial. It was retrospective, so no patient's care depended on the software. Experts' image readings were the reference standard. The 95% confidence interval for the specificity gain ran from -0.48% to 9.65%. NMPA said that it will strengthen post-marketing surveillance of the product.

benefit: Dr.Wise AI Lung Cancer helped doctors rate risk of lung nodules on CT
developer or vendor: Beijing Deepwise (北京深睿博联科技有限责任公司)
AI tool: Dr.Wise AI Lung Cancer (肺结节CT图像辅助诊断软件)
deployment context: Beijing Deepwise (multi-reader trial with 400 subjects at three sites); Three trial sites that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: area under the ROC curve for suspected malignant lung nodules rose from 0.7325 to 0.8397
what the sources leave unknown: The evidence is the maker's own paired reader study, in which doctors read stored chest CT scans of 400 subjects from three sites with and without Dr.Wise AI Lung Cancer. The reference was expert reading, with no outcome follow-up, and the report does not say that any patient's care depended on the software. CMDE restricts it to trained doctors and excludes screening.

benefit: HIBA offers multilingual health information in Lebanon and Jordan
developer or vendor: Humanitarian Engineering Initiative, American University of Beirut
AI tool: HIBA Health Information Bot Assistant
deployment context: Lebanon and Jordan
what the sources leave unknown: The team used feedback from testing groups of 6, 20 and 50 participants to refine language, usability and content. The team reports about 700 queries over six months and use in shelters in Lebanon. No measured change in health knowledge, decisions or health has been reported. Support for 28 languages does not establish comparable accuracy, safety or accessibility in each language.

benefit: CAFEIN trains research models without centralizing sensitive data
AI tool: CAFEIN federated-learning platform
deployment context: CERN; European clinical centers in the TRUSTroke stroke project
what the sources leave unknown: The only measured result is a model comparison on a public stroke dataset, in which federated training with federated averaging performed better than training on local data alone. No source quantifies an analytical gain for a partner institution or a resulting patient outcome. The makers describe model inference as planned.

benefit: A smartwatch alert leads a 34-year-old to treatment for a weakened heart
developer or vendor: Not stated (the report does not name the device's maker)
AI tool: Smartwatch arrhythmia detection (brand and model not stated)
deployment context: Göttingen, Germany
use-case relevant outcome: radiofrequency ablation restored his ejection fraction to 50% at six months
what the sources leave unknown: The authors name neither the watch nor the form of its alert, so a learned AI component is not established. The watch's contribution is the initial trigger. Recovery followed clinical investigation, medication and ablation, and no source measures how much earlier the alert led to care. The authors of a later review note that premature atrial contractions are a major source of false-positive atrial fibrillation alerts on smartwatches.

benefit: Viz HCM flags hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in a 61-year-old
AI tool: Viz HCM
deployment context: Cleveland Clinic; Cleveland, United States
sample: Cleveland Clinic, Cleveland, Ohio, with 103,492 ECGs in 45,873 patients from 19 February 2024 to 1 November 2024.
use-case relevant outcome: by week 8 the resting gradient was 9 mm Hg
what the sources leave unknown: The AI score triggered referral, but the diagnosis came from echocardiography and the physiological response from medication. The case report ends at week 8, so durable outcomes are unknown. In the hospital program, 691 of the 1,265 flagged patients had an alternate diagnosis, and reviewers at the U.S. Food and Drug Administration found a low positive predictive value.

benefit: AI yoga instructor recognizes ten poses in tests, with no user trial
developer or vendor: Centre for Development of Advanced Computing, Pune
AI tool: AI-based Virtual Yoga Instructor
deployment context: not in the sources
what the sources leave unknown: The authors report that their classifier identified ten yoga poses with an accuracy of 0.86 on test data. They report no trial with practitioners. Nor do they report a fitness or health result or compare the instructor with a human instructor.

benefit: Rapid LVO may cut the time to report stroke scans by 8.6 minutes
AI tool: Rapid LVO (RapidAI)
deployment context: Stroke center at the University of California, Irvine (cohort study by Soun and colleagues); Orange, California, United States
what the sources leave unknown: The turnaround figure rests on one before-and-after study at a single US stroke center, with no adjustment for confounding, which Canada's Drug Agency rated low certainty. Effects on door-to-intervention times and on patients' function were very uncertain. The agency found no evidence on patient harms and no cost-effectiveness study.

benefit: uAI-AorticDissection flagged aortic dissections in China's review
developer or vendor: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence Co., Ltd. (上海联影智能医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: uAI-AorticDissection (主动脉夹层CT血管造影图像辅助分诊软件)
deployment context: Shanghai United Imaging Intelligence (retrospective trial with 380 subjects at three institutions); Three trial institutions in China that the report does not name
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own, a retrospective single-arm study of stored images from three institutions, with 184 of 380 subjects positive. It excluded poor images and patients with aortic ulcer, intramural hematoma, aneurysm, rupture or earlier aortic surgery or endovascular treatment. An expert panel's reading was the reference. No doctor read the images with and without the software.

benefit: ChatGPT helps review MRI literature on intravascular lymphoma
AI tool: ChatGPT using GPT-4o
deployment context: Affiliated Yuebei People's Hospital of Shantou University Medical College; Shaoguan, Guangdong, China
what the sources leave unknown: The authors do not report time saved or another outcome for anyone. The authors' own case report is the only source, and no independent assessment of the review that ChatGPT assisted is on record.

benefit: Medicare contractor covers AI-QCT plaque analysis for chest pain
AI tool: AI-enabled CT-based quantitative coronary topography and coronary plaque analysis (AI-QCT/AI-CPA), chiefly Cleerly's platform, with HeartFlow plaque analysis also in the evidence
deployment context: Medicare providers performing coronary CT angiography in Palmetto GBA's jurisdictions; Alabama, Georgia, Tennessee, South Carolina, North Carolina, Virginia and West Virginia, United States
use-case relevant outcome: changed management plans for 57.1% of 750 patients
what the sources leave unknown: CERTAIN had a short follow-up and was not designed to compare the software-guided approach with standard care. DECODE was small, had no control group and did not know how changed plans affected patients. CLARIFY had no control group and took three expert readers as ground truth. Most studies did not represent Medicare patients by age. Oregon's HERC staff said no effect on health outcomes had been shown.

benefit: CADTH finds that AI-assisted colonoscopy may detect more adenomas
AI tool: AI-assisted (computer-aided detection) colonoscopy systems, including Deep-GI and CAD EYE in the included trial
deployment context: Endoscopy services in the studies that CADTH reviewed; Multiple countries (studies), with guidance for Canada
what the sources leave unknown: One CADTH reviewer screened, appraised and summarized the five included studies, and the summary gives no effect sizes. Not every included study found statistically significant differences in adenoma detection, adenomas per procedure or miss rates. The one trial did not test Deep-GI against CAD EYE statistically. No included study measured colorectal cancer incidence or deaths.

benefit: An automated diabetes prevention app did as well as human coaches
AI tool: Sweetch AI-led Diabetes Prevention Program app
deployment context: Johns Hopkins Medicine AI-DPP study (sites in Baltimore and at Reading Hospital, Tower Health); Baltimore, Maryland, and Reading, Pennsylvania, United States
sample: 368 adults with prediabetes and overweight or obesity at two US sites.
use-case relevant outcome: 31.7% of the AI group and 31.9% of the human-coaching group met the combined goal
what the sources leave unknown: not checked

benefit: HW-ES helped endoscopists miss fewer colon polyps in a trial
developer or vendor: Changsha Huiwei Intelligent Medical Technology Co., Ltd. (长沙慧维智能医疗科技有限公司)
AI tool: HW-ES (肠息肉电子下消化道内窥镜图像辅助检测软件)
deployment context: Changsha Huiwei Intelligent Medical Technology (prospective randomized trial with 354 patients at three sites); Three trial sites that the report does not name, for a registration in China
use-case relevant outcome: missed 12.41% of polyps, against 50.80% without it
what the sources leave unknown: The trial was the maker's own, a prospective, stratified randomized, single-blind, sequential superiority trial at three sites with 354 patients. CMDE reports lesion-level miss rates and says that the software's output is for reference only and must not be the sole basis of a clinical decision. No outcome of care for any patient is reported.

benefit: Grok flags a displaced wrist fracture that urgent care missed
AI tool: Grok chatbot (xAI) on X, image analysis of an uploaded wrist X-ray
deployment context: X Corp (Grok on the X platform); United States
what the sources leave unknown: No clinical record or independent review of the original image is public, and the post's words “distal radial head” are unclear. The casting fits the treatment that she reports, but her account does not show that Grok prevented surgery. In two studies in 2026, Grok 4.1 detected 39.6% of distal radius fractures, and Grok 3 correctly diagnosed 18.8% of fracture images.

benefit: ForeSight-HF drafts heart-failure advice for two nursing-home patients
developer or vendor: ProviderLoop (New York) with Mount Sinai clinicians
AI tool: ForeSight-HF (large-language-model clinical decision support on the ProviderLoop platform)
deployment context: Skilled nursing facilities served through the ProviderLoop platform (location not stated); New York, New York, USA (authors)
sample: Two patients with heart failure in a skilled nursing facility, chosen to show contrasting Forrester hemodynamic quadrants.
what the sources leave unknown: The authors give no evidence that the model directed either patient's treatment. No prospective effect on treatment or health was tested. As of 29 October 2026, Europe PMC listed no trial, follow-up report or citing article on ForeSight-HF.

benefit: AI may have helped Abu Dhabi surgeons separate twins joined at the head
developer or vendor: XRlabs (implant design, per its own release); the hospital names no developer for the planning tools
AI tool: XRlabs 'Surgical Intelligence' platform for AI-designed skull implants (identified only by the vendor) and unnamed 'AI-enhanced surgical planning' (PureHealth statement)
deployment context: PureHealth - SEHA Sheikh Khalifa Medical City, Abu Dhabi, with Gemini Untwined (Professor Noor Ul Owase Jeelani); Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates
use-case relevant outcome: successful separation in four staged procedures
what the sources leave unknown: No source compares the result with planning without AI, and no clinical evaluation separates the model's contribution from the surgical team's work. The reports differ on the twins' age and on the timing of the operations, and they give no exact operation date. XRlabs gives no clinical follow-up interval.

benefit: Willem, Cardiologs and ILR-ECG-A cut heart monitors' false alerts
AI tool: Willem (IDOVEN), Cardiologs and ILR-ECG-A (Implicity), AI algorithms that re-read insertable cardiac monitor recordings
deployment context: Remote monitoring centers in the studies that Avalia-t reviewed: Valley Hospital in the United States (Cardiologs), one center in Italy (IDOVEN) and 31 US and French centers on the Implicity platform; Spain (assessment), with studies in the United States, Italy and France
use-case relevant outcome: removed between 60.3% and 98% of the monitors' false positives
what the sources leave unknown: Avalia-t rated the four diagnostic studies at high risk of bias, and employees, shareholders or advisers of the makers co-wrote them. Two studies shared patients, and the IDOVEN study had 20. The monitors studied were older models. No evidence covered clinicians' time saved or costs. Avalia-t could draw no conclusion on clinical impact.
